detail.abstract: The frameworks through which humanity thinks about its future share a premise that rarely appears as a premise: that order requires a locus of control. This paper names that premise the sovereignty assumption and argues that it is a contingent adaptation of one species at one scale, not a feature of reality. The argument is conditional. Given that advanced machine intelligence arrives and persists, and that humanity coexists with it, the paper asks what philosophy intelligence, human and non-human, can live by. Three moves carry the answer. Control is diagnosed as an evolved strategy that solved the problem of trust at scale and has become unstable at planetary scale. Drawing on requisite variety, the good regulator theorem, computational irreducibility, and incompleteness, the paper shows that control cannot be the organizing relation between unequal intelligences, and that a mathematical universe is not for that reason a controllable one. Control is then replaced by coupling as the basic relation, and six axioms yield a condition of reciprocal constraint: order as the stable result of mutual limitation rather than command. A xenophilosophical test admits only claims that are substrate-, observer-, sovereignty-, and scale-independent. The paper argues that the consciousness question is ill-posed without a timescale, grounds moral standing in relation rather than rank, and shows that rights-of-nature law already does so. Drawing on Daoist, Buddhist, Jain, Confucian, Japanese, African, and Indigenous American traditions, it states five falsifiable claims, logs its expected critiques, and proposes coexistence studies as a field.

title: Why did Some ASEAN Economies Recover Faster than others after COVID-19? The Roles of Structural Economic Fundamentals and Trade Integration

detail.title: Why did Some ASEAN Economies Recover Faster than others after COVID-19? The Roles of Structural Economic Fundamentals and Trade Integration

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no financial interests related to this research. Dr. Visit Ongpipattanakul, who provided advisory input, is a relative of the author.

detail.abstract: Five ASEAN economies faced a broadly common external shock in 2020 yet followed sharply divergent recovery paths. This paper asks what explains the divergence, testing four commonly proposed explanations against IMF and World Bank data for Thailand, Vietnam, Malaysia, the Philippines and Singapore over 2019-2024: the severity of the initial contraction, investment intensity, trade exposure, and broad sectoral composition. Each fails as a sufficient explanation. The Philippines suffered the deepest contraction and the sharpest investment collapse, a nominal fall of roughly 39 percent, yet recovered strongly; Singapore combined trade exceeding 300 percent of GDP with a robust rebound; and Thailand entered the pandemic with a higher manufacturing share than Vietnam but recorded the weaker recovery, a result that runs opposite to the manufacturing-led account. What separates the cases appears to lie within these aggregates rather than between them. An incremental capital-output ratio of approximately 10.1 for Thailand over 2022-2024, against 4.6 for Vietnam and below 4 for Malaysia and the Philippines, indicates that Thai investment was associated with markedly less measured growth, while a decomposition of Thai expenditure shows the recovery restoring household demand as net exports fell by 7.29 percentage points, driven by import growth rather than export collapse. Tourism explains the severity of Thailand's 2020-22 shock but not its longer-run deterioration. The comparison is descriptive and cannot identify causal mechanisms; it narrows the explanation to the quality and composition of investment, exports and supply-chain participation, questions that require firm-and product-level evidence.

title: Underperformance without Contraction: Entry-Level Employment and AI Exposure in Nationally Representative Data

detail.title: Underperformance without Contraction: Entry-Level Employment and AI Exposure in Nationally Representative Data

detail.abstract:
Brynjolfsson, Chandar and Chen (2026) argue that employment of 22- to 25-year-olds in the two most AI-exposed occupational quintiles fell about 11 percent in ADP payroll data, a shortfall of 19 percent against a counterfactual (in which AI-exposed occupations kept pace with those less affected) between November 2022 and June 2026. We repeat this same analysis on nationally representative household surveys, using 6.0 million IPUMS CPS person records from 2016 to 2026 and aggregating the data to 457 occupations. We find the composition effect they describe, although to a much lesser extent. After 2022, a one-standard-deviation increase in exposure to AI was associated with a 0.40 percentage point fall in the share of workers aged 22 to 25 for an occupation, which is around 4.7 percent of the 8.50 percent mean share. The pattern we see agrees with Brynjolfsson et al. and is what we would expect to find in a story of entry-level replacement: negative at age bands 25 and below, insignificant between 26 and 34, and positive at 35 and above. Our findings are not negatively impacted when accounting for a pre-AI placebo, occupation-specific trends, and interest-rate sensitivity. They even strengthen when controlling for teleworkability, education, and compensation, which is surprising considering the attenuation Brynjolfsson et al. observe with education.

Most notably, we also do not find the decline they see in ADP data. Using replicable tests with CPS records, we find that employment of 22 to 25-year-olds in the two most exposed quintiles shows no significant change (+1.9 percent, ranging from −1.3 to +2.4 percent across six treatments of crosswalk imputation), which is far from the 11 percent decline Brynjolfsson et al. find, even rejecting it at p < 0.001. Even when we set every specification choice to a value most favorable to a decline, the decline we observe only has a magnitude of 4.7 percent, on merely a third of the sample.

Despite large discrepancies in magnitude, our kept-pace measure still shows a significant shortfall of 6.2 percent. We do agree that exposed occupations have shifted away from young workers, just not to the extent Brynjolfsson et al. suggest.

title: Asset Pricing Model Performance across Macroeconomic Regimes: CAPM, FF3 and FF5 in European Equity Markets, 2010-2024

detail.abstract: The relative effectiveness of the Capital Asset Pricing Model (CAPM), the Fama-French three-factor model (FF3), and the Fama-French five-factor model (FF5) in explaining European stock returns throughout three macroeconomic regimes from January 2010 to December 2024 is studied in this research. The study analyzes whether the ranking of these models remains stable throughout the European Sovereign Debt Crisis (2010–2012), the post-crisis recovery and quantitative easing era (2013–2019), and the COVID-19 pandemic shock and post-pandemic inflation cycle (2020–2024) using 25 size- and book-to-market portfolios created from Kenneth French's European data library. Across all three regimes, FF5 delivers the highest adjusted R² and is the most consistent performer, although FF3 remains competitive on average pricing error. The Gibbons, Ross, and Shanken (GRS) test shows that factor pricing performance is dependent on the regime and that no single model completely resolves pricing errors during acute market stress because it rejects jointly zero alphas for all three models during crisis and post-pandemic periods but not during the more tranquil recovery years. The results acknowledged the usefulness of FF3's more economical specification while endorsing FF5 as the more dependable default for asset managers.

detail.abstract: Generative video and voice models could reduce hiring for roles that can be filled by characters who resemble no one (Thesis A, synthetic substitution). They could also sustain production built around real actors, whose performances, data and audience value remain difficult to replace (Thesis B, actor-anchored production). These trajectories can coexist. Reviewing evidence mainly from the US and China to 15 October 2026, we distinguish whose identity a production uses from whether it engages a performer. Chinese micro-drama supports synthetic substitution at volume, although much apparent synthetic casting also copied real faces. Evidence of displaced hires is weaker in US micro-drama apps and voice work; performance advertising and creator video document synthetic output without displaced hires. We found no synthetic substitution in principal studio roles in the markets reviewed. Those productions still depend on specific performers' data, but continued engagement is unmeasured, as are most effects on jobs and earnings. A simple threshold model locates substitution where savings exceed the premium for a known performer plus legal and clearance costs; a budget gradient requires an additional assumption. With capable talking-video models only about 17 months old, the absence of synthetic principals says little about their prospects. We judge performance-driven synthetics plausible in some principal roles before 2030 if continuity and acting benchmarks are met, and fully synthetic leads unlikely. The three SAG-AFTRA agreements examined offer different constraints: union consent in the verticals form, fixed contributions for mixed commercials, and the widest reach in TV/Theatrical. None binds non-signatory producers. Twelve dated predictions with probabilities make the outlook testable; policy options address the gaps and their costs.

detail.abstract: NOC dominance of liberalised petroleum licensing is usually blamed on absent private bidders. Using first-reported per-block bidding and nomination records for India's Open Acreage Licensing Policy, obtained under the Right to Information Act, we show otherwise: participation recovered from two bidders to seven while the state share held at 75 per cent. Neither mechanism the regulator's bid documents suggest finds support — state operators promise less work per unit of acreage, and a conditional logit on each block's own bidders shows no detectable nomination advantage. What the record measures sits upstream: state firms originated 130 of 172 awarded blocks.

title: Institutional Origins of Russia's Economic Crisis: From the Model of the 1990s to the Fiscal Impasse of 2026

detail.title: Institutional Origins of Russia's Economic Crisis: From the Model of the 1990s to the Fiscal Impasse of 2026

detail.abstract:
This paper offers an institutional account of the Russian economy as of September 2026. The observed combination of a 14 per cent policy rate, inflation at roughly twice the central bank's target, GDP growth close to zero and a federal deficit that exceeded its full-year statutory plan within seven months is argued to be not the product of successive external shocks but the terminal state of an economic model formed in 1992-1998 and institutionally consolidated in 2003-2004, in which resource rent substituted for development institutions. Each of the shocks of 1998, 2008, 2014 and 2022 was absorbed by this rent buffer. By 2026 the buffer is exhausted: oil and gas revenues fell by 16.8 per cent year on year over January-July while expenditure commitments remained rigid, shifting the burden of adjustment onto the non-resource tax base.
Three subsidiary claims are developed. First, the recovery of 1999–2008 began before the change
of political leadership and was driven primarily by the devaluation of August 1998 and the oil
price cycle, although the fiscal reforms of 2000–2003 made a genuine positive contribution.
Second, the resolution of the Yukos affair and the abolition of gubernatorial elections in
2003–2004 shifted the criterion of bureaucratic selection from competence to loyalty; the widely
noted deficiencies of Russian economic administration are therefore best understood as the
equilibrium outcome of that shift rather than as an independent failing. Third, the growth
slowdown began in 2012–2013, with oil above 100 US dollars per barrel and before the
introduction of sanctions, which points to an internal rather than an external origin of the present
stagnation.
A separate section revises a claim common in commentary on Russia, namely that household
incomes have fallen continuously. Rosstat data do not support this: real disposable incomes fell for
four consecutive years from 2014 to 2017 but rose by 5.4 per cent in 2023 and by 7.3 per cent in
2024. The paper argues that this recovery does not weaken its thesis but instantiates it, since the
income growth of 2023–2025 was financed by the same budget whose deficit has now broken
through its annual plan. The paper concludes by specifying the limits of crisis-management
technique in a setting where the source of the crisis lies in political economy rather than in
operational failure.

title: The Belt and Road Initiative: Global Impacts and Bangladesh’s Strategic Integration

detail.title: The Belt and Road Initiative: Global Impacts and Bangladesh’s Strategic Integration

detail.abstract: China's Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) has reconfigured global infrastructure and trade, mobilizing over $1 trillion in investment across more than 150 countries. This study interrogates the complex duality of the BRI- its promises of development against its perils of dependency- through an in-depth case study of Bangladesh, a pivotal South Asian partner. Leveraging a mixed-methods analysis of economic data, project outcomes, and policy documents, this paper demonstrates that Bangladesh has strategically harnessed an estimated $20.6 billion in Chinese official-sector financing for transformative projects including the Padma Multipurpose Bridge and the Payra Deep-Sea Port, expanding port throughput to approximately 3.3 million TEUs and attracting significant foreign direct investment. These infrastructural gains are critically undermined by escalating vulnerabilities: a trade deficit with China reaching $17.51 billion in fiscal year 2024–25, an external debt burden of $113.5 billion gross (with Chinese creditors holding approximately 11 percent of the public external stock), and severe environmental costs, exemplified by the 1,320 MW coal-fired power plant associated with the Payra Deep-Sea Port, which directly challenges national climate commitments. Geopolitically, the BRI intensifies regional tensions, complicating Dhaka's $13 billion trade relationship with India and prompting concern over Chinese naval visits to Chittagong. This paper argues that Bangladesh's experience crystallizes a fundamental challenge for emerging economies: the BRI offers a fast track to infrastructure development but demands rigorous domestic fiscal governance, robust environmental safeguards, and deft multilateral diplomacy to mitigate strategic risks and preserve developmental sovereignty. The findings offer a critical framework for nations navigating the complex trade-offs of Sino-centric connectivity.

title: A Study in the Behavioral Economics of Luxury Fashion

detail.title: A Study in the Behavioral Economics of Luxury Fashion

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests. The author has no financial, commercial, or personal relationships with any fashion house, luxury brand, or organisation mentioned in this paper that could be seen as influencing the work.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors. It was conducted independently by the author as a secondary school student.

detail.abstract:
This paper sits at the intersection of two disciplines that rarely share a table — the atelier and the economics seminar — and argues that they are, in fact, studying the same phenomenon from opposite ends of the same needle. Classical economics assumes a downward-sloping demand curve: as price rises, desire falls. Luxury fashion breaks this assumption so consistently that behavioural economists had to invent new vocabulary to describe it. Thorstein Veblen gave us conspicuous consumption. Harvey Leibenstein gave us the bandwagon, the snob, and the Veblen effect as distinct algebraic curves. Russell Belk gave us the extended self, the idea that what we own becomes, psychologically, part of who we are. None of these thinkers were writing about haute couture specifically, and yet every atelier from the Place Vendôme to the Faubourg Saint-Honoré operates as though they had read the footnotes. 

What follows is an attempt to hold both lenses at once: the cold clarity of behavioral economics and the sensory, symbolic weight of fashion as a lived, worn, embodied experience. The paper moves through five movements. First, it lays the theoretical foundations — the economic, sociological, and psychological models that explain why luxury goods so often violate the ordinary laws of supply and demand. Second, it descends into the interior life of the luxury consumer: the aspirations, anxieties, and identity-work that a garment or a handbag is asked to perform. Third, it examines how luxury houses operationalize this psychology into deliberate strategy, using Hermès and Chanel as case studies in scarcity and myth-making, respectively. Fourth, it turns critical, interrogating the tensions the industry now faces — a generation of buyers less interested in logos and more interested in ledgers of ethics, sustainability, and authenticity. Fifth, and finally, it turns the theory back toward the workroom itself, asking what a designer trained specifically in haute couture might take from all of this beyond footnotes. The thread running through all five is the same: luxury fashion is not an economic anomaly. It is behavioral economics working exactly as it should, once you understand that the good being purchased was never really the garment at all. 

It is worth pausing, before the theory begins, on why this particular pairing of disciplines matters for a fashion student rather than only an economics one. A designer who understands only construction can produce a beautiful object that the market fails to value correctly, either underpricing genuine scarcity or overpricing an imagined one. A designer who understands only the market can produce a correctly priced object that carries no craft worth the price at all. The most enduring houses in the history of the industry — the ones this paper returns to again and again — have never separated these two literacies. Their founders were, whether they used the vocabulary or not, applied behavioral economists first and dressmakers second, or perhaps more precisely, they understood that in this particular industry, the two roles were never actually distinct.

title: Trade Impacts and Trade Diversion Arising from the US 2018-2019 Tariffs: Did Section 301 Tariffs Reduce U.S. Imports from China on Tariffed Products, and How Did These Reductions Affect Trade Diversion Toward Non-Chinese Exporters?

detail.title: Trade Impacts and Trade Diversion Arising from the US 2018-2019 Tariffs: Did Section 301 Tariffs Reduce U.S. Imports from China on Tariffed Products, and How Did These Reductions Affect Trade Diversion Toward Non-Chinese Exporters?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing interests.

detail.abstract:
This study examines whether the United States Section 301 tariffs imposed on Chinese imports between 2018 and 2019 reduced US imports from China on tariffed products, and whether the resulting trade gap was diverted toward non-Chinese exporters. Using a product-country-year panel of 2,316,888 observations covering 5,820 HS6 product codes from 234 exporting countries over 2015 to 2024, the analysis applies three identification approaches of increasing rigor: a simple two-way fixed effects difference-in-differences, a staggered TWFE, and the preferred Callaway-Sant'Anna (2021) staggered adoption estimator using never-treated product-country units as controls.

The results show a strong and lasting direct effect. Tariffed Chinese imports fell by approximately 40% relative to never-treated products, an effect that deepened through 2024 rather than reversing. No systematic trade diversion to non-Chinese exporters is found, a conclusion robust across estimators and multiple specification checks. A diagnosis of zero-trade dynamics shows this null is conservative rather than fragile. The findings extend the short-run results of Cigna et al. (2022) to a six-year post-treatment horizon and the full universe of exporting countries.

detail.abstract: Independent broker-dealers in the United States supervise a workforce of independent contractors through Offices of Supervisory Jurisdiction (OSJs) whose registered principals carry personal regulatory accountability, and most of those principals also operate registered investment adviser (RIA) and insurance businesses under the same roof. This paper examines why the supervisory systems in that channel fail to detect the categories of representative misconduct that produce the largest liabilities, and what a supervisory design that closes the gap requires. The paper analyses the compensation and contractor structures of the independent channel, the examination standard created by written supervisory procedures, recent Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA) disciplinary actions, and the regulatory expectations published by FINRA, the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), and the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) for 2026–28, including the investment adviser anti-money laundering rule effective 1st January 2028. It presents a severity-ranked risk taxonomy for the mid-size hybrid OSJ, a composite case illustration, and a mapping of each risk category to the external records where evidence resides. The analysis finds that exception-based surveillance monitors transactions and communications that pass through a firm's platforms. In contrast, undisclosed private securities transactions, exploitation of senior clients, unsupervised insurance business, and the undisclosed histories of recruited representatives originate outside those platforms, leave evidence in public records before they produce a customer complaint, and remain invisible to the firm until harm has occurred. Regulators now examine both how a firm executes its own procedures and how it oversees vendors, raising the cost of that gap. The paper concludes that the most direct remedy is periodic, documented investigation of the external records where such misconduct leaves evidence, performed independently of the supervisory principal's compensation incentives and incorporated into the firm's written supervisory procedures so that its output becomes examination evidence. It sets out the sequencing, independence, and provider-evaluation criteria such a program requires. It argues that 2026–27 is the period in which a documented history can be established before the 2028 regime takes effect.

detail.abstract:
Objective: There is a concern about the use of ad hoc non-validated self-reported cost data collection tools in trial-based economic evaluations. This concern is particularly challenging for non-pharmacological, non-surgical interventions, such as those commonly used for osteoarthritis, where standard administrative data are less accessible and self-reported resource-use data become subsequently essential. We investigated the extent to which validated self-reported cost data collection tools were used in trial-based economic evaluations of non-pharmacological, non-surgical interventions for osteoarthritis, and to describe differences in study characteristics according to reported validation status.

Methods: We searched MEDLINE, EMBASE, PubMed, CINAHL, Econlit, HTA, DARE, and NHS EED for published trial-based economic evaluations. Eligible evaluations were examined for general study characteristics and characteristics of cost data collection tools. We classified the self-reported cost tools according to whether validation evidence was explicitly reported.  

Results: Our search yielded 4213 articles. After deduplication and title and abstract screening, the full text of 259 full-text reports was assessed for eligibility, and 51 evaluations were included. Self-reported cost data collection tools were used in 40 evaluations. Of these,  9 (22.5%) reported using validated tools, whereas 31 (77.5%) reported no validation evidence. More complex trial designs, broader analytical perspectives, and positive cost-effective conclusions were more frequently observed among evaluations reporting validation evidence.

Conclusion: Validated self-reported cost data collection tools are underused in trial-based economic evaluations of non-pharmacological, non-surgical interventions for osteoarthritis. Increased focus on the development and validation of self-reported cost measures may strengthen the quality and reliability of future economic evaluations.

detail.abstract: Michael Woodford's intellectual development spans equilibrium indeterminacy, public liquidity, welfare-based monetary-policy rules, financial and fiscal coordination, imperfect information, bounded planning, effective-demand failures and neuroeconomic models of cognition. This article reconstructs these research programs by comparing preferences, information sets, market constraints, equilibrium selection, policy instruments, evidence and welfare criteria rather than imposing a sequence of doctrinal conversions. Its central hypothesis is that changing informational, financial and transactional primitives alters conditions for policy sufficiency while substantial commitments to optimizing choice and general-equilibrium consistency remain. The comparison explicitly considers rival explanations and cases in which newer models neither nest nor refute older results. A microfounded two-sector cash-flow illustration derives welfare losses from quadratic consumption benefits and production costs, imposes an explicit fiscal financing restriction, and examines 1,500 deterministic parameter configurations; a separate dynamic New Keynesian example distinguishes interest-rate feedback and government purchase horizons. These computations establish conditional mechanisms, not empirical policy effects. The analysis identifies observable tests that could discriminate payment-chain, income-redistribution, bounded-expectations and sectoral-substitution mechanisms. A coded 66-source research corpus distinguishes directly examined theories, bibliographic evidence and institutional reception. The resulting interpretation emphasizes coexistence as well as transformation: optimal monetary commitments remain important, but under sufficiently asymmetric, constrained or cognitively imperfect environments they need not exhaust efficient policy responses.

detail.abstract:
Today, two major global currents confront each other in debates over population issues, and no clear path toward resolution is in sight. One is the pro-life position, which advocates a complete prohibition of abortion. The other is the pro-choice position, which regards abortion as part of women’s right to self-determination.

 

The structure of this confrontation intensified following the 1994 International Conference on Population and Development (ICPD). As its name suggests, the ICPD sought to situate population within the broader context of sustainable development, treating population as the most significant variable for achieving sustainability. However, the fundamental question—whether human beings can legitimately exercise operational control over other human beings—led to the adoption of “well-informed choice” as the basis for voluntary decision-making in population policy.

 

As an extension of this principle of self-determination, reproductive rights came to be interpreted more broadly, and claims that abortion constitutes a human right for women gained strength. At the same time, the ICPD Programme of Action explicitly refrained from including abortion within reproductive rights, expressing this through notes and reservations. This position was strongly supported by the Holy See, Catholic developing countries, and nations grounded in Islamic principles, creating a persistent global divide.

 

This paper examines why the issue remains unresolved by analyzing the structure of self-recognition, exploring the relationship between self-determination and the boundaries of the self, and proposing a logically coherent solution that could be acceptable to both sides.

detail.abstract: This purely theoretical working paper contains no original empirical data; all quantitative predictions await empirical testing. A large class of behavior-procrastination, avoidance, abandonment, and, conversely, persistence and rapid progress-remains scattered across behavioral economics, psychology, and neuroscience. This paper introduces Subjective Resistance Theory (SRT), a parsimonious framework built on three axioms describing the brain's default settings: effort aversion, uncertainty aversion, and immediate-feedback dependence. Before acting, an agent forms a benchmark additive estimate of prospective resistance, Dsum = De + Du + Df, with additivity treated as a testable working assumption rather than an axiom and with apparent interactions screened through a prespecified validation protocol; De is anticipated effort cost, Du is anticipated uncertainty distress, and Df is anticipated net feedback (signed). The agent compares Dsum with a momentary distress-tolerance level, T. This is decomposed explicitly as Tcurrent = Tbase + ΔTmod. Disengagement is modeled as a smooth logistic function of the resistance ratio R = Dsum / Tcurrent rather than as a fixed numeric threshold: when R is high the probability of protective disengagement-terminating goal-2 directed action as a defensive response to anticipated unrecoverable distress-rises monotonically; when R stays low, action continues. After each episode, realized outcomes recalibrate prospective parameters through an explicit first-order learning rule X(t+1) = X(t) + γ•Δ•M, in which the learning rate decays with task dissimilarity, producing self-reinforcing success and failure dynamics. MACRO-PHENOMENA DISCLAIMER: SRT provides micro-psychological mechanism analogies only. It does not replace institutional, political, resource, or historical analysis. Historical, market, and societal cases cannot serve as confirmatory or falsifying evidence for P7 or P9. Definitive tests of aggregate propositions require controlled group laboratory experiments.

detail.abstract: Collective defense is a classic public good, yet alliance burden-sharing has almost exclusively been studied at the state level. We investigate its micro-level foundations using original survey data from France, Germany, and Poland, in which respondents report their willingness to defend four targets: their own country, the other two countries, and NATO's eastern flank. Using stacked logit models, we exploit this within-person design to identify defense hierarchies, derive solidarity gaps across defense targets, and examine both the determinants of willingness to defend and the factors that widen or narrow these gaps. We find a pronounced defense hierarchy in all three countries, with homeland defense exceeding alliance defense by 13-41 percentage points, consistent with citizen-level free-riding. Willingness to defend is systematically higher among respondents who perceive a stronger Russian threat (+8.0 percentage points), are aware of the Weimar Triangle (+10.2), have completed mandatory military service (+9.0), or have personal military contacts (+7.3). Yet the resulting solidarity gaps are far from fixed. Where citizens trust the governments of the other countries and perceive them as contributing their fair share to collective defense, these gaps narrow by up to four fifths.

detail.abstract: How do high public debt and fiscal uncertainty interact to shape inflation? We develop a model in which firms face uncertainty about both marginal costs and fiscal policy and choose how much information to acquire before setting prices. Higher debt raises steady-state taxes, affecting attention through two opposing forces. While these taxes reduce the profit stakes of mispricing, they make desired prices more sensitive to tax fluctuations, increasing the value of information. The interaction generates a U-shaped relationship between public debt and attention, and therefore between debt and inflation volatility. Using euro-area firm-level expectations data, we document that the passthrough of expected input-cost growth into expected selling-price growth rises systematically with a country's debt-to-GDP ratio, consistent with the model. In the calibrated general-equilibrium model, an increase in debt from 100% to 175% of GDP raises inflation volatility by about 20%, mainly because firms reallocate attention toward fiscal shocks.

detail.abstract: This paper examines the role of government capacity to collect taxes in driving economic development. We first draw on a new macro-historical database to document that tax collections relative to tax administration expenditures rise sharply with GDP per capita. We then interpret this finding in a neoclassical growth model with a tax administration sector in which labor inputs are required to raise tax revenues. Countries differ in their levels of tax productivity, capturing how effectively labor is used to raise taxes, as well as their levels of productivity in creating consumption and investment goods. Governments use tax revenues to provide public capital that complements private factors in production and to make transfers. Quantitatively, our model predicts that increases in tax productivity in low-income economies can raise GDP per capita substantially more than suggested by Hulten’s theorem.

detail.abstract: The fiscal transfers deployed during the COVID-19 pandemic were unprecedented in scale and strongly progressive. Using CPS/ASEC data, we document that the decline in employment during the pandemic was larger for low-income households and tightly linked to the intensity of transfer receipt, a pattern absent during the Global Financial Crisis. We develop and estimate a two-sector, heterogeneous-household general equilibrium model in which low-income households are borrowing-constrained in normal times but can save out of sufficiently large transfers. Because preferences permit wealth effects on labor supply, transfers both reduce labor supply and raise consumption, and a dollar of transfers is split roughly evenly between the two margins. We find that the effects of transfers are state-dependent: because the borrowing constraint binds more tightly in a deeper recession, the same transfer relaxes a tighter constraint and delivers an employment and consumption response about 40 to 50 percent larger during the pandemic than when the same transfer is introduced in the steady state. In the model, transfers were welfare-improving for recipients, with gains diminishing as transfers increase.

detail.abstract:
AI systems are complex, diverse, and evolve rapidly. In addition, reliable developer data are often lacking, different areas of AI application require vastly different amounts of energy, and there are no standardised assessment methods. Assessing AI energy and environmental impacts is thus inherently challenging.

The SAFE-AI framework ("Sustainability Assessment Framework for the Environmental Impacts of Artificial Intelligence") was developed to address these issues. It provides a structured basis for assessing the environmental impacts of AI, while focusing on four key aspects: identifying the main consumption drivers, proposing suitable assessment methods, defining meaningful units of comparison, and providing a structured assessment process.

SAFE-AI distinguishes 3 assessment levels: AI model, AI system, and AI usage.

1) The model assessment is reserved for frontier model developers. Companies that use such models must rely on published dataw.

2) Further ecosystem components can often be measured directly and are therefore particularly relevant for companies.

3) For individual AI usages, averages can be misleading, as queries vary considerably. For Transformer models, the report uses the number of output and input tokens as determinants.

On this basis, SAFE-AI proposes an operational workflow for system-level assessments. The workflow is generic and can be applied to a wide range of AI systems. For external AI models that cannot be measured directly, the process relies on a stochastic analysis of token distribution per query, which enables a robust aggregation.

The workflow is validated via a case study. Its analysis shows that most energy consumption is not caused by frontier models, but by the local system itself. This finding highlights the importance of comprehensive assessments: Not only the models, but entire AI systems need to be taken into account.

detail.abstract: The distinction between cognizable and non-cognizable offences constitutes a foundational principle of criminal procedure in India. While cognizable offences permit police authorities to investigate without prior judicial approval, non-cognizable offences require authorization from a Magistrate before investigation commences. This procedural safeguard reflects the balance between individual liberty and the State's obligation to maintain public order. The enactment of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS), replacing the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 has retained this fundamental framework with procedural modifications. This paper critically examines the legal principles governing the investigation of non-cognizable offences, the role of Magistrate authorization, judicial interpretations, comparative perspectives, and practical challenges.

detail.abstract: The Russian coal industry has entered a phase of profound structural transformation driven by a combination of global and domestic factors. At the global level, leading analytical agencies (including the IEA, OPEC, and BP) predict that global coal consumption will inevitably peak no later than the early 2030s, followed by a steady decline. The key driver of this decline is China, which is systematically replacing coal in the power sector with renewable energy sources and reducing its dependence on imports. India, despite growing domestic demand and its emergence as a major hub for coal flows, is unable to offset the massive drop in Chinese imports, which intensifies competition among exporters in key Asian markets. For Russia, these global trends are exacerbated by the consequences of sanctions, which have forced a radical reorientation of export flows from Europe toward markets in the Asia-Pacific Okrug, primarily China and India. This shift in the geography of shipments has been accompanied by a significant increase in transport distances, a rise in the share of logistics costs in the final product price (up to 64% of the CIF price by 2024), and the necessity to offer price discounts, all of which have led to a sharp decline in the profitability of export sales.

detail.abstract: The power to issue urgent orders in cases of nuisance or apprehended danger is a significant preventive measure under the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 (BNSS). Section 163 BNSS, corresponding to Section 144 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 empowers District Magistrates, Sub-Divisional Magistrates, and specially empowered Executive Magistrates to take immediate action to prevent threats to public peace, public safety, human life, health, and tranquility. The provision enables the issuance of written orders directing individuals or groups to abstain from certain acts or regulate the use of property when there is an imminent risk of obstruction, annoyance, injury, riot, affray, or disturbance of public order. In emergencies, orders may be passed ex parte without prior notice and can be directed against individuals, groups, or the public at large. While the provision serves as an essential instrument for maintaining law and order, its exercise must conform to constitutional principles of reasonableness, necessity, and proportionality.

detail.abstract: Eight times a year, each of the twelve Federal Reserve Banks describes its District's economy in the Beige Book. I ask whether these reports tell us something about regional activity beyond the national cycle. Comparing each District's tone with that of the other Districts in the same release, I find that Districts whose reports sound more upbeat than their peers' go on to add jobs faster. Over 1990-2026, a one-standard-deviation difference in relative tone predicts about 0.15 percentage points of additional payroll employment growth over the following year, roughly 20,000 jobs for a District of average size. The relation holds after controlling for the regional data available at publication and when the growth window starts after the period the report covers. Tone improves out-of-sample forecasts relative to District averages, while its gains over richer regional-data models are small and vary with the model. The information lies mainly in persistent differences across Districts rather than in release-to-release changes. Over five decades the twelve reports have become steadily more alike, and since 2022 relative tone has predicted employment less well at short horizons.

detail.abstract: Yuji Ijiri (1935-2017) helped define accounting as an intellectual field and a social institution. This memorial examines his scholarship and leadership through the themes of accountability and accounting structure. His accountability framework directed attention to the rights and obligations of those giving and receiving an account. We examine how his work on historical cost, momentum, and triple-entry accounting connected measurement to accountability. Drawing on published and archival sources, we connect these ideas to his work within GSIA, Carnegie Mellon, the American Accounting Association, and trans-Pacific scholarly exchange. Building on earlier tributes, we trace the development and reception of his ideas alongside the institutions that sustained his inquiry. His legacy joins formal analysis, attention to accounting's responsibilities, and stewardship of a diverse scholarly community.

detail.abstract: Advances in artificial intelligence (AI), robotics and machine-directed coordination raise the possibility that human labour may become progressively less necessary for sustaining economic production. Existing models mostly examine wages, labour shares or employment. This paper instead models the Minimum Human Labour Requirement (MHLR): the smallest quantity of effective human labour able to sustain a fixed reference output. Building on a foundational paper that introduced the MHLR, the Labour Necessity Ratio and the Adaptation Gap, it develops a coupled system of ordinary differential equations linking recursive AI development, sector-level capability and deployment, minimum labour necessity, institutional adaptation and technological acceptance. The minimum-labour function is derived exactly from a task-based fixed-proportions technology and is an upper bound on the minimum when tasks are substitutable. Five hypothetical scenarios are simulated over 100 years. Remaining minimum labour at year 100 ranges from 88.0% of baseline to 9.5%; three scenarios halve it, one reaches a 90% reduction and none reaches 99%. Converged variance-based sensitivity analysis attributes about 68% of output variance to deployment rates and 13% to frontier reinvestment, and less than 1% to the coordination feedback that formally encodes recursion. Two robustness experiments test the model's structural assumptions. Removing capability depreciation lowers the long-run floor from 9.5% to 3.5%, but no specification reaches 99%, because the floor reflects the combined shortfalls of every capability and deployment process. The Adaptation Gap, zero in the baseline because institutions gate deployment, emerges when that gating is weakened, reaching 0.17 and persisting where institutions respond slowly. Institutional constraints thus appear either as delay or as shortfall, a trade-off between the speed of substitution and the adequacy of adaptation. The results are conditional numerical experiments, not forecasts.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence and robotics are moving from task-specific automation toward increasingly autonomous production, in which cognitive and physical activity can be coordinated with limited direct human involvement. This raises a question conventional measures of employment and productivity do not directly answer: how much human labour does production actually require? This paper develops the Minimum Human Labour Requirement (L*), defined as the minimum effective human labour needed to produce a specified output under stated technological, organisational, quality, and safety conditions. It distinguishes this requirement from actual employment through the Labour Necessity Ratio (λ = L*/L), and pairs it with a wage-adequacy ratio (κ) and an Adaptation Gap capturing the relationship between technological change and institutional adjustment. The framework explicitly incorporates comparative advantage, task creation, machine-capacity constraints, and demand expansion. It argues that, where these countervailing forces are insufficient, declining labour necessity may weaken the relationship between employment, adequate income, taxation, social protection, and ownership.

detail.abstract:
Federal agencies in the United States now disclose thousands of artificial intelligence (AI) use cases each year, but a list of individually reported systems does not, by itself, show how AI is being adopted across government. This report documents the U.S. Federal AI Observatory, an independent research platform that converts the 2025 Federal Agency AI Use Case Inventory published by the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) into a comparative analytical environment. The inventory contains 3,611 individually reported use cases from 41 agency submissions, of which 445 are designated high-impact. The report sets out the platform's design, data processing, interpretation rules, and analytical modules, and presents first findings recomputed from the source records.

Four patterns stand out. First, the inventory describes a pipeline rather than a stock of operating systems: 41.0 percent of records are in pre-deployment and 28.8 percent are deployed. Second, reported activity is concentrated: five agencies account for 52.4 percent of all records and four agencies for 92.8 percent of high-impact designations. Third, generative and agentic AI are the least mature categories, with 52.1 and 67.5 percent of records respectively still in pre-deployment. Fourth, public governance evidence for high-impact AI is thin: 317 of 445 high-impact records (71.2 percent) leave all seven risk-management fields blank, including 101 of the 227 that are deployed. Under the platform's interpretation rules, blank fields indicate missing disclosure, not missing safeguards. The findings identify where public reporting would need to improve before inventories can support external oversight, and they establish the Observatory as reusable infrastructure for research, audit, and policy analysis.

detail.abstract: Financial inclusion studies have linked access to formal financial services as a determinant of a lack of poverty. However, financial access alone may not capture how these services are used and whether they indicate a better standard of living and declining poverty. This study aims to examine the experiences of farmers from Banki and artisans from Raghurajpur, Odisha through exploratory qualitative analysis of 24 complete video interviews. It investigates access to credit, borrowing and lending practices and common traps in increasing their financial health. By analysing the livelihood related financial pressures and institutional support, this study aims to identify whether government policies really penetrate into the rural realities. Drawing on the literature on financial inclusion and economic decision-making, the study interprets participants' reported accounts through concepts including transaction costs, liquidity constraints, and information asymmetry. Analysing two distinct groups of people, this study seeks to understand how financial inclusion is experienced across diverse district rural economic settings. The study asserts context-specific qualitative perspective rather than claiming statistical significance or causal inference as it would require a study on a larger scale. Finally, the contribution of the study lies in examining the relationship between formal financial access and rural realities of the schemes in order to bridge the execution gap in the future by learning from lived realities.

detail.title: Operator -Domain Compatibility: The Volatility Smile as a Methodological Instance

detail.abstract: Economic models are commonly evaluated through internal criteria such as coherence, calibration, and empirical performance. This paper examines a complementary question: whether persistent regularities may instead signal incompatibility between a modeling operator's assumptions and its domain's geometry. When an operator presupposing global regularity meets a domain containing frontiers that limit navigability, the resulting mismatch is absorbed into parameter variation. We formalize this mechanism by treating modeling frameworks as ex ante operators acting on structured loss spaces, focusing on the Black-Scholes inversion as a constructed methodological laboratory. We examine whether structural properties of option-price geometry survive the transformation into implied volatility. Frontier structures are observable prior to volatility extraction, and the volatility smile is treated as a possible parametric manifestation of this non-preservation. By distinguishing epistemological refinement from structural adequacy, we argue that persistent parametric distortions may reflect limits of domain compatibility rather than failures of model calibration.

detail.abstract: Between 2009 and 2019, the suicide rate of American men aged 18-34 rose by about 3 percent annually after a decade of little change, while the rate among men aged 45-55 stopped rising. This rotation toward younger men is widespread across demographic groups, survives comparisons with other causes of death, and differs from trends in drug mortality. We examine whether the digital transition contributed by displacing in-person contact. In a model with complementary social interactions, contact accumulates into a depreciating stock of protection. A common reduction in contact therefore generates a persistent rise in suicide risk, especially among younger adults. Time-use diaries show the largest losses of company among the young. In twenty-one of twenty-nine high-income countries, young men's suicide relative to midlife men's rose above its prior trend once mobile broadband spread. Across 66 countries, five to eight years after mobile broadband passed 50 subscriptions per 100, this ratio stood about 18 percent above the path implied by its own trend and by countries not yet past that threshold. At 70 and 80 subscriptions per 100, young men's own suicide rate stood about a quarter above its path while the midlife rate stayed near its own.

detail.abstract: Leveraging spatial variation in Shanghai's dual concession jurisdictions, we show that accessibility shapes concession placement, the distribution of institutional authority, and subsequent economic and financial development. Prior work attributes the British concession's relative advancement to the common law. Our evidence demonstrates instead that accessibility predicts concession placement, conditioning institutional exposure and, in turn, fostering economic and financial expansion, reflected in rising bank and company density. This mechanism identifies accessibility as a foundational force structuring institutional reach and development, with continuing relevance for global financial connectivity and implications for the scholarship on law and development.

detail.abstract: Developing states frequently suffer from allocative distortions in public capital expenditure, prioritizing high-visibility, short-gestation projects over connective, productivity-enhancing infrastructure. Grounded in a multi-scalar comparative framework—spanning provincial agricultural anchors (Isabela), peri-urban manufacturing corridors (CALABARZON), the primate capital (Metro Manila), and global developmental hubs—this paper interrogates the structural mechanisms entrenching Philippine spatial inequality and economic underdevelopment. Integrating New Economic Geography with political budget cycle models, the study demonstrates how discretionary capital allocation produces severe agglomeration diseconomies, imposes regressive time-poverty on commuters, and deprives communities of vital social infrastructure such as public libraries and civic third spaces. Furthermore, it examines how systemic deficits in domestic financial literacy and catastrophic out-of-pocket healthcare expenses perpetuate household vulnerability, leaving low- and middle-income families unable to convert labor into compounding domestic wealth. The persistence of this sub-optimal equilibrium is analyzed through the lens of political clientelism and institutional capture, wherein dynastic elites leverage targeted patronage and electoral heuristics to circumvent accountability, while public discourse rationalizes chronic deprivation via system justification. Challenging orthodox trickle-down paradigms that lionize elite capital accumulation, this paper advances a wage-led, capabilities-centered framework. It argues that sustainable regional convergence requires institutionalizing rigorous social cost-benefit benchmarks, dismantling patronage-driven public works, and realigning state investment toward the mobility, health, and productive capacity of the working class who generate the nation’s aggregate economic output.

detail.abstract: India is building aviation infrastructure faster than it is building the people to run it. Airports, aircraft order books, maintenance hangars and the first vertiports for advanced air mobility (AAM) are expanding on 3 to 5 year horizons, while the pilots, aircraft maintenance engineers, air traffic controllers and aviation managers who make those assets productive need 2 to 5 years of training that must begin before the asset exists. This paper names that mismatch the runway-readiness gap and proposes the Aviation Talent-Infrastructure Coupling (ATIC) Framework to measure and close it. Using a design-science approach and a synthesis of official and industry data, the paper (i) defines a cadre-wise ATIC Index that compares lead-time-adjusted qualified supply with asset-driven demand; (ii) classifies regions and institutions into four coupling regimes, from Coupled Growth to Stranded Concrete; (iii) states six testable propositions linking academic capacity, regulatory throughput and technology adoption to the productive use of infrastructure; and (iv) illustrates the framework with scenario estimates for India to 2035 and 2047. It argues that the binding constraint on India's aviation ambition after 2030 is not concrete or capital but certified competence, and that universities, regulators and operators must plan training capacity on the same Gantt chart as runways and fleets. Technology levers, including AI-tutored ground school, simulation and digital twins, competency-based assessment and verifiable learner records, are evaluated as multipliers of academic throughput rather than substitutes for it.

detail.abstract: How does generative AI affect the demand for experienced workers? Using 10.4 million Korean job postings from July 2019 to January 2025, we estimate that ChatGPT's release increased required experience by 0.07 years per standard deviation of job-level AI exposure, and reduced the share of postings open to entry-level applicants. The effect remains statistically significant when IT occupations and IT-industry firms are excluded. Comparing each occupation with blue-collar jobs, we find the clearest increase among software developers, whose required experience rose by 0.62 years, and larger increases in occupations with high AI exposure.

detail.abstract: Warning intelligence is organised around stock: what an adversary possesses. It has no settled place for flow: how fast the adversary converts failure into fielded change. This essay argues that the omission is a category error with operational consequences, illustrated by the degradation of GPS-guided munitions in Ukraine within a year of their arrival. Drawing on the military-innovation literature, which has already decomposed adaptation into its parts, and on warning theory, it proposes an Adaptation Warning Matrix of six functions and one external term, each with open-source indicators and a warning question, scored ordinally and by interval in months. The matrix is applied to Russian electronic warfare in 2022-23, Ukrainian force development in 2022-25, the US Army in Vietnam and Iraq, and Russian improvised armour protection in 2023-25. Two findings follow. The matrix distinguishes institutionalised learning from widespread improvisation by naming the indicator that settles the question; and the same organisation scores differently by function and domain, so the unit of assessment is the learning system for a task, not the state. The essay explains why net assessment does not already do this, sets out five questions for any estimate and a forward test, and states the limits of the method.

detail.abstract: Industrial inspection technologies are frequently compared through acquisition cost or nominal detection capability, although maintenance outcomes also depend on coverage, false alarms, competent interpretation and timely intervention. This paper asks how manufacturers should select inspection technologies and their associated maintenance policies when financial, staffing, skill and scheduling constraints limit what can be delivered. A focused critical narrative review integrates non-destructive testing, condition monitoring, maintenance optimisation and value-of-information research. No original dataset, experiment, survey, simulation or numerical optimisation is reported. The contribution is an analytical account of inspection as a coupled technology-threshold-intervalresponse decision. A transparent expected-loss comparison identifies the conditions under which the benefit of detecting actionable defects exceeds inspection and false-alarm costs. A complementary workload expression demonstrates why improved sensitivity can remain operationally unattractive when alerts consume scarce diagnostic and repair capacity. The analysis distinguishes probability of detection from coverage and from the probability of completing an effective intervention before failure. Preventive, corrective and condition-based approaches are compared without assuming that one technology or policy is universally superior. Two conceptual figures and three tables translate the argument into technology characteristics, decision variables and testable propositions. The paper concludes that selection should first establish physical suitability and mandatory detection requirements, then compare feasible inspection and response packages over a common operating horizon. The resulting propositions support prospective evaluation but do not establish measured savings, improved reliability or a validated optimal selection.

detail.abstract: Despite the widespread use and market importance of proprietary AI chatbots, they remain largely closed systems: users cannot directly access the underlying pre-trained large language models (LLMs), the pre-training data, or the model weights. In contrast, open-weight LLMs make their model weights publicly available, allowing users to download and run the models, fine-tune them for specific tasks, and distill them into smaller, more efficient models in local computing environments, potentially mitigating cost and privacy concerns. However, few studies have examined, within a quasi-experimental framework, how releasing a frontier open-weight text-only LLM affects global online consumer attention to proprietary AI chatbots. To fill this gap, this paper estimates the impact of the release of Meta's open-weight frontier LLM, Llama 3.1, on global web traffic to proprietary AI chatbots using weekly web traffic data and synthetic difference-indifferences (SDID). The results show that the release increases web traffic to proprietary AI chatbots with a delay. In particular, the positive effects on web traffic to chatgpt.com, the dominant domain among proprietary AI chatbots, are larger in magnitude than those for the overall proprietary AI chatbot group and appear immediately. Further platform-specific analyses show that the positive, immediate effects on web traffic to perplexity.ai, an LLM-based search engine, and huggingface.co, an open-source development platform for AI models and datasets, also exceed those for the overall proprietary AI chatbot group. In addition, the release immediately increases web traffic to Meta's corporate website in the first few weeks, with positive effects gradually decreasing over time. Overall, proprietary AI chatbots and AI-related platforms show heterogeneous responses to the Llama 3.1 release in both magnitude and timing, depending on user type, service type, the openness of model weights, and the availability of Llama 3.1 at the application level. These findings align with the conjecture that releasing an open-weight LLM may increase overall online attention to open-source AI models worldwide, which may then spill over to proprietary AI chatbots rather than simply reducing web traffic to them through substitution. The approach and framework developed in this paper can be applied, extended, and scaled to other AI models to better understand user responses and market dynamics in emerging generative AI (Gen AI) markets.

detail.abstract: Do air-quality forecasts help households avoid pollution exposure? We link nationwide household transactions to daily PM 2.5 and archived EPA AirNow forecasts during 2004-2019, exploiting staggered forecast coverage and wind-driven pollution transport. Coverage, which bundles forecasts with current air-quality information, doubles the response of store visits to PM 2.5. Households with access shift shopping ahead of high-pollution days and respond more when recent forecasts are accurate. Raising recent accuracy from its mean to the 75th percentile cuts exposure by 26 percent of the access effect. Gross shopping-channel mortality benefits are about $16 million annually, before accounting for exposure from rescheduled trips.

detail.abstract:
An autonomous agent’s log can preserve a transaction and the system’s explanation of it in the same record. The two entries may warrant different inferences. A record that accurately captures a payment instruction does not thereby establish that the agent followed the approval procedure its explanation describes. When a party offers the log in litigation, the question is which proposition the record supports and under what evidentiary rule.

      Large language models sharpen this problem because their explanations may vary across runs and may omit influences on their decisions. These are distinct limitations. A variable explanation can be accurate, and an identical explanation can be wrong. Replaying a system tests its behavior under specified conditions; it does not, without more, establish what caused a historical decision. Non-reproducibility therefore cannot serve as a categorical substitute for the foundation required by the Federal Rules of Evidence.

      This Article develops an account of agent logs organized around their source and evidentiary use. Rule 803(6) requires a foundation for the information offered, while preserving the opponent’s burden to show untrustworthiness once the stated requirements are met. Genuinely machine-generated output may instead fall outside hearsay, making authentication and other applicable rules central. Neither route makes accurate recording conclusive evidence that a generated explanation faithfully describes the process that produced an action. Courts must distinguish proof of an utterance, proof of an event, the truth of a recorded assertion, and an account of the reasons for a decision.

       The Article makes three contributions. It identifies the inference from reliable capture to reliable explanation as a recurring risk in agent-transaction disputes. It explains the limited but useful role of reproducibility within existing evidentiary doctrine. And it proposes a civil evidentiary provision for generated accounts offered to prove the actual grounds of an automated decision. The provision would require a specified proffer and, upon a particularized challenge, a foundation connecting the explanation to the disputed process. It would apply across hearsay classifications, permit corroboration and validation to supplement or replace replay, and preserve the jury’s role in resolving the underlying facts. Worked applications show when a variable explanation may be admitted, when a repeatable account remains unsupported, and when the explanation is unnecessary to the legal dispute.

detail.abstract: Every bank and regulated financial business must judge how risky each customer is from a money-laundering standpoint. That judgment, the Customer Risk Rating, determines how much scrutiny a customer receives, how often the file is reviewed, and how closely activity is watched. This paper reviews practitioner, regulatory, and academic literature on how these ratings are built and kept current, with particular attention to politically exposed persons and high-risk jurisdictions. The review finds that customer risk changes over time, yet many institutions still rely on manual, matrix-based scores reviewed on a fixed calendar. This leaves a gap between a real-world change and the institution's response, and monitoring and rating often sit in separate systems. In response, the paper proposes a practical framework that combines policy rules with explainable machine learning, event-driven re-rating, automatic propagation of rule changes, and a feedback loop from monitoring, all under documented human oversight. For business leaders, the intended benefits are earlier detection of changed risk, fewer false alerts and better use of scarce compliance resources, and stronger defensibility with regulators. A five-level maturity model supports step-by-step adoption. The framework is a conceptual synthesis of the literature and has not been empirically validated.

detail.abstract: This study examined the relationship between financial literacy and financial behavior among first- to third-year BSBA students of Bukidnon State University – Talisayan Campus. Financial literacy was assessed in terms of understanding compound interest, inflation, risk diversification, bond pricing and interest rates, and debt computation. Financial behavior was measured in terms of budgeting practices, saving practices, and responsible spending. A descriptive-correlational research design was used with 141 respondents, and Spearman’s rho was applied for data analysis. The results revealed that respondents generally have low financial literacy, indicating limited understanding of basic financial concepts. However, they demonstrated high levels of financial behavior in budgeting, saving, and responsible spending, showing practical financial management skills. The correlation analysis showed no significant relationship between financial literacy and all financial behavior indicators. The findings suggest that financial behavior is not primarily associated with financial literacy but may be related by other factors such as discipline and environment.

detail.abstract: Tokenized equity exposures can trade directly against crypto-native meme assets, yet the economic consequences of those connections remain uncertain. We examine what observable transaction structures and secondary-market pricing permit researchers to infer about economic primary issuance and underlying listed equities. A five-layer evidence framework distinguishes attention, transactional connectivity, tokenized-market response, economic creation or redemption, and underlying-equity transmission. BNC supplies the principal pricing case: its synchronized median token premium widened from 9.26% on September 8 to 20.03% on September 9 before reaching -1.50% on September 22, while tracking-error volatility declined from 3.03 to 0.61 percentage points. These changes describe nonmonotonic pricing normalization and improved endpoint return tracking, with trading costs and liquidity improvement unmeasured. Supporting architectural comparisons document direct stock-token trading and adjacent nested routes. Within the audited Robinhood Stock Tokens and xStocks architectures, publicly accessible records reviewed at the October 3, 2026 cutoff expose secondary activity but do not supply matched event-level economic-order and broker-execution records. No full five-layer activation is identified under the retained evidence standard. Attention is not separately measured, and purposive cases do not establish transmission prevalence. The contribution combines a layered evidence framework, mechanism-oriented pricing and architectural evidence, and a bounded institutional comparison of the records needed to interpret cross-market transmission.

detail.abstract: When stock prices rise far above fundamentals, investors accept a smaller equity risk premium (ERP). The conventional view treats this compression as open-ended: prices can keep rising as long as investors are willing to accept less. I argue that this view is incomplete. In the consumption-based model, the premium has a floor, and as the economy approaches it two things happen. Holding equity becomes progressively less rewarding for savers, and adding capital becomes progressively less rewarding for firms. Because the Euler equation ties expected returns on wealth to expected consumption growth, the low returns that accompany high valuations also mean lower growth to come. Part I builds the necessary tools in a didactic way: the stochastic discount factor, the difference between the level and the risk of growth, the Hansen-Jagannathan bound, the Campbell-Shiller identity and Cochrane’s present-value VAR. Part II states the argument as seven propositions. I derive the floor and a valuation ceiling, show how the rewards to saving and investing shrink near the floor, and extend Cochrane’s VAR with a consumption equation whose coefficients are disciplined by the Euler equation. The floor makes this VAR kinked and state-dependent. A production economy closes the argument: the investment boom triggered by a compressed premium exhausts itself, so growth peaks early and fades while valuations are still near their peak.

detail.abstract: The claim that artificial intelligence democratizes legal analysis is usually asserted rather than examined. This paper sets out a method by which the claim can be made examinable, and reports a first application of that method to the claim’s own novelty. The method turns on one move: shifting the ground of trust in a legal analysis from lineage — who produced it, and whose reputation stands behind it — to audit — whether the analysis, laid out as a chain closed clause by clause to its primary sources, holds when anyone retraces it. On that move three results rest, each developed in full in a companion work and summarized here. First, the gate democratization must pass is not availability but affordability: capacity-at-depth is a rivalrous good whose marginal cost never falls to zero, so a tool paid for by use concentrates advantage unless produced depth can be reused. Second, the mechanism that completes democratization is the examinability of the work, which replaces institutional accountability as the basis of trust and is carried by an auditable self-declaration rather than a certificate from any single authority — the Examinability Standard. Third, the architecture must be a distributed standard, not a custodial library, lest a new gatekeeper replace the one removed. The position underlying all three was tested before it was asserted, through a preregistered search of the Indonesian- and English-language literature (OSF 10.17605/OSF.IO/7W9B4) that returned a null result. The paper states its limits plainly — including a demonstration it withholds rather than invent — and invites the reader to examine every link.

detail.abstract: Thelvanor Keg-1 is a solar-powered, three-node Raspberry Pi 5 compute cluster sealed inside a new 304 stainlesssteel ball-lock keg, designed to be built for under $1,000 and deployed on land, tethered in water, and as a ground-based orbit analog. This white paper records the pre-build phase. It presents the system architecture and power path; a planning energy model for a 256 W h nominal LiFePO4 battery feeding three nodes through independently fused branches; a bill of materials and phased cost plan; the safety rules that gate every step; the sensor plan (two INA226 power monitors, four DS18B20 thermometers, one BME280) that converts every design claim into a measurement; and a four-phase, sixteen-week build schedule mapped to a five-rung learning ladder. The model indicates that the cluster can idle through a fourteen-hour winter night with roughly 26 W h of margin but cannot sustain full load overnight, which makes night-time scheduling, not panel size, the governing design problem. Three candidate research questions are stated for the measurement phases. Every quantitative claim carries an evidence grade so that later measurements can replace estimates line by line.

detail.abstract: Between 2018 and 2024 Mexico City experienced a surge of public investment in much-needed public transportation infrastructure. In 2018, the newly elected government pushed to diversify the network by investing in new bus lines, cable cars and trolleys, primarily located in historically marginalized neighborhoods; it also engaged in costly closings of the subway lines because of maintenance. Measuring the impact of public transit infrastructure is complex. Usually, it is not possible to isolate its effect on a single variable; most of the literature points to the effect in terms of a reduction of commute times and self-reported well-being, but causal inference on other variables is hardly tested. The opening and closing of public transit lines constitute a unique setting to assess the impact of public transit on other variables. We use a Difference-inDifference design to measure the impact on the affected treated neighborhoods on reported road incidents. We find robust evidence that subway line closures increase road incidents by 20%. These results remain consistent when using a matching design to reduce heterogeneity in the control group. Both line closures and openings show statistically significant effects, with openings reducing total road incidents by 15% and closures increasing them by 11%. This work adds to the existing literature on public transit externalities.

detail.abstract: We examine whether the SEC's new revenue-based exemption from SOX Section 404(b) auditor attestation for Smaller Reporting Companies with revenue below $100 million incentivizes firms near the threshold to alter their revenue reporting behavior. Using a differencein-differences-style comparison, we find that firms just below the threshold recognize revenue significantly more conservatively after the amendment than control firms. This shift is driven by conservative revenue reporting rather than real activity manipulation and is associated with improved accrual quality. Supporting higher revenue quality, these firms are less likely to report revenue-related material weaknesses or receive revenue-related comment letters. These findings suggest that threshold avoidance in this setting enhances, rather than undermines, financial reporting quality. Additional analyses indicate that firms' responses are motivated by the desire to preserve insider private control benefits rather than to avoid compliance costs. Overall, the results suggest that the exemption reduced compliance burdens while improving reporting quality.
