detail.abstract: This paper presents an exploratory case study of adaptive intraday risk management in the leveraged semiconductor ETFs SOXS and SOXL on October 15, 2026. Using timestamped five-minute chart snapshots, platform-classified money-flow data, and broker order records, the study reconstructs how a discretionary trader revised the relative relevance of three pre-selected historical scenario families-continuation, consolidation, and reversal-as live evidence unfolded. In SOXS, an opening low of 45.575 was followed by a high of 48.370 and subsequent lower lows of 45.420 and 45.170. Combined with the loss of short-term moving-average support and weakening classified flow, these observations increased the weight of the reversal scenario and led to the cancellation of a resting limit buy at 45.150. Later prices crossed the cancelled order levels, creating a path-based counterfactual rather than a realized outcome. On the paired instrument SOXL, three completed round-trip trades generated a combined gross price-spread profit of USD 16.60 before fees. The contribution is an auditable record of real-time scenario revision and exposure management under uncertainty. The study does not claim statistical validity, predictive superiority, or generalizable performance. Limitations arising from purposive case selection, discretionary analog weighting, and incomplete contemporaneous documentation are explicitly acknowledged.

title: Beyond Shareholder Exclusivity: Board-Level Worker Participation as a "Drop of Socialist Oil"

detail.title: Beyond Shareholder Exclusivity: Board-Level Worker Participation as a "Drop of Socialist Oil"

declarations.declarationOfInterest: nothing
declarations.funderStatement: none

detail.abstract:
Corporate law ordinarily assigns board selection to shareholders and protects employees through institutions outside corporate office. Board-level worker participation qualifies that allocation by making labor a basis for membership in a corporate governing or supervisory body. Its historical association with industrial democracy has often given the intervention a political significance greater than its immediate legal effect.

This Article argues that shareholder predominance does not require shareholder exclusivity. Through the European and American histories of participation, it examines arrangements in which labor supplies a route to office while private ownership and common corporate responsibility remain intact. 

The comparison separates the constituency selecting an officeholder from the authority exercised once appointed. It also shows why representation cannot be evaluated by counting seats alone: institutional location, selection, activation, and the relationship to collective bargaining affect what the arrangement does. The American statutory and negotiated exceptions remain marginal, but their existence qualifies the claim that labor-based access is inherently incompatible with the ordinary unitary board.

The Article then examines the authority to introduce participation. An enabling mechanism controlled by the corporation differs from an entitlement that employees can activate, even when neither produces representation automatically. Non-adoption remains relevant evidence, but must be interpreted against the existing allocation of governance rights and the circumstances in which representation is negotiated. These findings do not establish a general case for compulsion or the economic superiority of worker directors. They identify a bounded nonproprietary principle within proprietary corporate governance. In this sense, the “drop of socialist oil” consists in admitting labor to the constitution of corporate office without requiring the displacement of shareholders’ predominant position.

detail.abstract: We develop methods for estimating intraday networks from binary event observations and testing changes in their community structure over a fixed time span. We first establish max-norm consistency of local estimators and a stable central limit theorem for their fixeddimensional contrasts. Under a degree-corrected block model, row-normalized, unscaled signal eigenvectors yield a co-membership representation whose population value is invariant to activity and connectivity. We prove uniform community recovery on pure blocks and consistency of integrated co-membership, allowing supplied or consistently estimated counts to vary across regimes. For inference, we propose an event-level multiplier bootstrap, which provides asymptotically valid tests and simultaneous confidence bands for co-membership contrasts while accounting for dependence within event vectors and across shared blocks. Simulations illustrate the finite-sample performance of the proposed methods. Applications to stock price staleness compare local network weights and fitted groups around an exchange disruption and scheduled monetary policy announcements.

detail.abstract: Remote and hybrid work (RHW) has reshaped office demand and urban mobility, amplifying a "flight to quality" toward sustainable, amenity-rich urban buildings, while workers have concurrently dispersed farther from city centers. Using a proprietary dataset of the Canadian office market-one of the world's most RHW-intensive environments-we combine office market, sustainability, and mobility data to explore how building sustainability and urbanity relate to space use and commute distances. Findings show that areas with sustainably-certified or GRESB-participating office buildings record significantly more visits per square foot of office space. After offices reopened in mid-2021, commute distances fell more in high-RHW areas than elsewhere, consistent with fewer workplace trips. However, areas with more urban and sustainable features meaningfully attenuate this decline. In triple-differences estimates, these features have large, positive moderating effects that offset most or all of the RHW-related decline, implying longer average commutes where such offices concentrate. Case studies for Toronto and Calgary translate these estimates into added daily kilometers travelled and explore how shifts in commute mode could reduce associated emissions. When combined with the existing literature on RHW and office space use, results suggest that investment in urban and sustainable buildings may support office space demand and neighborhood vibrancy, yet with the potential unintended consequence of increased commute distances.

detail.abstract: In this paper I propose a quantitative theory for the dynamics of wealth inequality based on heterogeneous exposure to aggregate risk in asset returns. I develop an optimal portfolio choice model in which housing is a necessary good and households endogenously shift their portfolios towards riskier assets as they get wealthier. Since households are exposed to different sources of aggregate return risk, wealth inequality naturally responds to movements in asset returns. I show that return shocks have large and persistent effects on wealth inequality and that the model replicates the U-shape observed in top U.S. wealth shares since the 1960s.

detail.abstract: Ransom and Sutch attribute the high cost of postbellum Southern credit to merchant monopoly, while Higgs attributes it to a risk premium on lending against an uncertain cotton crop. This paper tests the monopoly account using the Gold Standard Act of 1900, which cut the minimum capital required to organize a national bank from $50,000 to $25,000 in places with 3,000 residents or fewer. If merchants held farmers in cotton by controlling credit, access to a competing lender should have reduced cotton’s share of farmland. I build a county panel for Alabama, Georgia, Louisiana, Mississippi, and South Carolina in the census years 1890, 1900, and 1910, and measure each county’s exposure to the reform as its count of incorporated places below the population threshold. With county and year fixed effects and standard errors clustered by county, each additional eligible town is associated with a 0.30 percentage point increase in cotton’s share of farmland in 1910 (p = 0.0006). The sign is opposite to the one the monopoly account predicts. The result fits Higgs’s argument that cotton remained central to lending because of its value as collateral, and it is also consistent with new bank capital financing additional cotton acreage. The estimate is a robust association, not a fully exogenous causal effect.

detail.abstract: This study examines monetary policy under competition between a centrally managed currency (the "Dollar") and a fixed-supply alternative (the "Peso"). Theory and laboratory evidence reveal two equilibrium types. In the pass-through equilibrium, Dollar inflation is high and trade effects are limited. In the substitution equilibrium, Dollar dominance rises and velocity falls, muting Dollar inflation while generating inflation spillovers to Peso despite its fixed supply. Which equilibrium prevails depends on self-fulfilling inflation beliefs, not policy alone, and Dollar trade shares reveal these beliefs. The central bank therefore faces a trade-off between Dollar dominance and inflation control.

detail.title: Four Foundations: The Test Result From Ontology to the Testing of Results

detail.abstract: A result is visible. Its foundation often is not. A building may stand for years, yet the fact that it stands is not proof that its foundation has been tested under stress. The same distinction applies beyond physical structures. Institutions, states, monetary systems, organizations, contracts, policies, and other constructed realities may produce observable results while their underlying foundations remain largely unexamined. This paper develops a framework for testing an existing result through four foundational dimensions: Iman, Mizan, Nizham, and Tartil. The framework emerged from a sequence of studies beginning with the Ontology of Money (Tamin, 2026a-g), followed by the examination of monetary trust, value, institutional guarantees, and ultimately the Ontology of the State. During that development, the four foundations appeared not merely as descriptive concepts but as a possible means of testing whether an observed result remains coherent when its underlying assumptions are subjected to stress. The purpose of this framework is not to replace financial audit, legal review, compliance, due diligence, scientific investigation, or institutional assessment. It asks a different question: Does the result remain ontologically coherent when tested against the foundations that are supposed to sustain it? Iman addresses the foundational condition of trust and commitment. Mizan addresses balance and proportional consequence. Nizham addresses the existence and coherence of order. Tartil addresses sequence, arrangement, and the integrity of progression. The central proposition is simple: the existence of a result establishes that something has occurred; it does not establish that the foundation producing that result is sound. The Four Foundations therefore provide a test from the visible result toward the less visible conditions beneath it.

detail.abstract:
In July 2025 it was reported that Grade 3 language proficiency in India had risen from 39 to 57 per cent, and mathematics from 42 to 65, between the National Achievement Survey (NAS) 2021 and PARAKH Rashtriya Sarvekshan (PRS) 2024. The figures govern how the sector reads NIPUN Bharat, and they divide the two state rankings in circulation: the Ministry's Performance Grading Index 2.0 uses PRS 2024, while the independent School Education Development Index declines it. This paper decomposes the comparison from published documents. It is not a psychometric equating; the item pools are unreleased.

Three findings. First, the comparison is one NCERT's own documents decline to authorise. The PRS 2024 Assessment Framework states that the round was designed "to establish a new trend line", and that "a comprehensive concordance analysis could determine whether trends between NAS 2021 and PARAKH Rashtriya Sarvekshan 2024 may be established." No such analysis is published. The reported figures appear in neither round's national report; they originate in a blog post of 19 August 2025 by PARAKH's chief executive, which in the same passage calls PRS 2024 a baseline.

Second, the headline is a property of band construction. On the one metric both rounds publish, the change is +2 and +3 points, and the Grade 3 Advanced threshold sits at +0.02 SD, the national mean, where a percentage-above-cut statistic is maximally sensitive to its own placement.

Third, the two rounds order India's districts almost independently: across 666 districts each round reproduces its own ordering across subjects at 0.92 and 0.94, the two rounds each other's at 0.30. The instability is programme-wide, not a 2021-2024 break.

No defensible Grade 3 trend can be stated. The remedy exists already, as Standard 5.20 of the Standards for Educational and Psychological Testing and as NAEP's long-term-trend instrument.

detail.abstract: Democracies are widely believed to protect the environment better than autocracies, but the evidence rests on cross-sectional comparisons and panel regressions that cannot separate regime type from what is correlated with it. We estimate the effect of democratization on carbon dioxide emissions using the 28 countries that experienced a democratization episode ending in a democratic transition between 1993 and 2017, identified from the Varieties of Democracy Episodes of Regime Transformation data and estimated with staggered difference-in-differences. Emissions per capita rise by about 18 percent on average after onset and by 25 percent by the sixth year, with no detectable pre-trend and nothing at placebo onsets. The average survives comparing each treated country only with countries in its own world region, but it is not uniform: it is concentrated in post-communist Europe and, less precisely, Asia, and is absent within Africa. No pre-onset characteristic of the inherited energy system, income or industrial structure systematically explains which countries respond. The increase runs mainly through the carbon intensity of the energy mix and not through income, although the decomposition is imprecise. Autocratization moves emissions in neither direction. As a secondary outcome, we find no statistically detectable improvement in population-weighted exposure to fine particulate matter and rule out improvements larger than about 12 percent, which is what the small share of fossil combustion in ambient particulate mass predicts.

detail.abstract: This paper examined the macro socioeconomic determinants of health outcomes in Nigeria between 1980 and 2015. The study was predicated on the Grossman analytical framework rooted in the human capital development theory. A macro-econometric model incorporating major macro socioeconomic variables in explaining health outcomes was explored. Two variants of the model were estimated based on alternative measures of health outcomes by life expectancy and under-five mortality. ARDL bound test estimation technique that took into consideration error correction mechanism was used. Tests of the model's reliability were carried out using unit root and Co-integration tests. Except for GDP per capita income, government health expenditure, and literacy rate had positive significant effects on life expectancy. The influences of government health expenditure was significant, but health worker exert positive influence though insignificant on under-five mortality rate. This suggests positive relationships suggested that they could be important in influencing health outcomes.

detail.abstract: When governments shield GDP from shocks, who absorbs the risk? This paper develops a trade framework in which fiscal responses change households' consumption and work effort. With public purchases financed by lump-sum household levies, sustaining output after adverse productivity shocks can require more work and less private consumption. These responses also change the relative prices that share risk through trade. In a one-sector benchmark with frictionless trade and no transfers, universal full GDP targeting removes this price insurance of labor returns to first order. In a quantitative application to China's 31 provinces, a partial GDP rule reduces national GDP volatility but raises volatility of private final demand-household consumption, investment, and inventories-and lowers welfare by 0.0271 percent of consumption under the baseline calibration. Yet much of this cost can be avoided by changing which shocks policy targets. At the same response strength, responding only to common sectoral shocks retains 89 percent of the national GDP standard-deviation reduction while reducing the welfare loss by approximately 73 percent, relative to a rule responding to both sectoral and regional shocks. Every province gains in welfare from this switch, although most experience less GDP stabilization. Stabilizing national output and stabilizing each province are therefore different policy objectives, with different household costs.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a novel structural credit risk framework that explicitly integrates climate transition risk into corporate debt valuation. Traditional structural models, such as the Merton (1974) framework, assume deterministic asset value dynamics and fail to capture sudden regulatory shifts, technological obsolescence, and carbonpricing shocks. By modeling firm asset values as a jump-diffusion process driven by stochastic carbon tax trajectories and carbon intensity metrics, we derive closed-form approximations for corporate bond spreads and default probabilities. Empirical calibration on highemission corporate sectors reveals that omitting climate policy shocks leads to a systematic underestimation of default risk by up to 34% over a five-year horizon. Our findings demonstrate that forward-looking climate-adjusted structural models are essential for accurate corporate debt pricing, capital adequacy assessments, and macroprudential stress testing.

detail.abstract: Green bonds outstanding are worth USD 2.9 trillion, and the evidence that their issuers then cut emissions rests on comparisons with similar firms that did not issue. Vendor emissions series follow changes in what a firm consolidates and how it accounts, so a divestiture at a comparison firm makes an unchanged issuer appear to raise its emissions, and an acquisition makes it appear to abate. For 289 first-time non-financial issuers from 2013 to 2022, screening the comparison firms' data moves the estimate by up to 17 log points, with a sign that depends on the comparison group. Against matched non-issuers, unscreened data make issuers' emissions appear to rise 13 percent; against firms that have just issued conventional bonds, they produce apparent cuts of 7 to 13 percent, as large as several published reductions. The distortion is traced to identifiable firms and events: HP's reported emissions fell 78 percent when Hewlett Packard Enterprise was separated. With both groups screened alike, no matched or local-projection design finds a significant reduction, and under parallel trends the most precise designs exclude net cuts above 2 to 4 percent. Issuance-year proceeds are 1.2 percent of assets for the median matched issuer, so proportional abatement would lower emissions by about 1 percent, below what firm-level data can detect. These conclusions rest on cleaning regimes that isolate each group's screens, firm-level forensics, placebo issuers and published designs. Applying the issuers' screens to the comparison firms requires no additional data and puts studies on a common footing.

detail.abstract: Which conclusions about the yield response to Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) news survive when the policy instrument is imperfect? We study nominal and real yields and inflation compensation around 92 FOMC meetings using an instrument constructed from changes in money-market rates around FOMC announcements. Because the instrument may also reflect nonpolicy news, we use historical benchmark data to quantify the resulting instrument error. Treating the instrument as valid, both nominal and real yields rise, with real yields rising more. Allowing the instrument to be imperfect, the evidence that both yields rise remains more robust than their ordering. This validation evidence therefore distinguishes which parts of the yield response continue to support a policy interpretation.

detail.abstract: Disaster losses create demands on public budgets for relief, reconstruction, and transfers, but how much of a loss becomes additional public spending depends on how recovery is financed. This paper examines how private insurance shapes that transmission. We provide a systematic, model-based account of uninsured disaster losses across countries and over time, combining reported insured losses with a Bayesian hierarchical model to estimate missing insured shares. Using these event-linked measures and local projections for up to 159 countries, we examine cumulative six-year fiscal responses. We find that disaster damage is followed by higher primary expenditure and that higher insured shares are associated with smaller expenditure responses, consistent with insurance reducing demands on the public budget. At average insurance coverage, the estimated public spending increase is nearly 80% smaller than for an uninsured disaster of the same size. The findings point to a potential fiscal dividend from private disaster insurance, suggesting that its contribution to disaster resilience extends beyond policyholders, to public budgets.

detail.abstract: We study how the U.S. stock market responds to presidential speech using about 15,800 spoken documents from 1993 to 2024 with exact delivery times and 469 major speeches from 1945 to 2024. A simple cheap-talk model predicts that, because the president always prefers higher prices, the tone of a speech carries no information, while formal addresses that disclose concrete policy raise the size of the market's move without predicting its direction. The evidence agrees. After a scheduled jointsession address, the absolute S&P 500 return on the next trading day is about 75 percent larger than usual, controlling for FOMC and employment-report days. Unscheduled addresses raise overnight absolute returns by about 56 percent. News conferences, interviews, radio addresses, and routine remarks have no effect, and no text measure predicts the sign of returns. The market listens when the president addresses the nation, but not to what he says.

detail.abstract: Governments across the developing world routinely cite macroeconomic stabilization (falling inflation, a steadier exchange rate, rebuilt reserves) as evidence that reform has succeeded, even where household and firm level conditions have worsened over the same period. This paper argues that the inference from aggregate stability to agent level wellbeing is a specific and nameable logical error, the fallacy of division: the attribution to the parts of a property that belongs only to the whole. Macroeconomic stability is an aggregate and, in important respects, an emergent property; it does not distribute automatically to the households and firms that make up the economy. Drawing on the stabilization and adjustment critiques of Cornia, Jolly and Stewart and of Killick, on Sen's distinction between output and capability, and on Bates's account of the political logic of policy choice in Africa, the paper develops a three-tier framework of macroeconomic, microeconomic and developmental stability; a transmission and feedback mechanism through which aggregate stabilization can coexist with, and at times produce, disequilibrium at the level of the agent; and a political economy account of why the error persists in institutional communication. Nigeria's 2023 to 2026 reforms serve as an illustrative case: IMF and World Bank documents record improved macroeconomic stability while the national poverty rate rose from 56 percent in 2023 to 63 percent in 2025. The paper concludes that persistent microeconomic disequilibrium is a potential source of future aggregate fragility, not a distributional footnote to successful stabilization.

detail.abstract: Institutional debt rollover lowers current maturity pressure, not economic cost; the cost changes only in when it arises and which sector bears it. This paper builds a closed, testable sub-model of that mechanism inside the FFTEI framework: two linked stock equations for total and deferred debt, a cost decomposition benchmarked on a shadow funding cost, a paired index (FFT EI, Λ), the second of which measures expected loss in deferred debt relative to loss-absorption capacity, and a weakest-link ceiling on the rollover share. Two propositions follow: maturity risk is converted into incidence risk, and debt sustainability is not capital efficiency. Both rest on the fact that rollover capacity is not loss-absorption capacity. The paper is positioned as a country-level realization of the Deferred Stability Illusion (DSI). A descriptive examination of China's local government debt shows temporal conditions and debt principal moving apart. Temporal conditions improved: the principal rollover ratio µ stayed at about 86-90% in 2019-2025, the average rate on outstanding bonds fell from 3.55% to 2.83%, and average remaining maturity lengthened from 4.4 years in 2018 to 10.5 years in 2025. Debt principal did not fall: legal debt rose from RMB 16.0 trillion at end-2015 to RMB 54.8 trillion at end-2025, and the repayment base grew about 4.6% a year against 13.1% for legal debt, with g B < g D in eight of ten years. Across 29 provinces the gap ∆ p = g Bg D is negative in every case and nearly uncorrelated with swap intensity (correlation about-0.10): swaps determine how much risk is deferred, not how much the repayment base deteriorates. Six firm-level mechanism cases illustrate the transmission.

title: Which Outcome Should Teach an LLM Reader? A Verified FOMC Benchmark and Reward-Design Evidence for Outcome-Guided Agents in Finance

detail.abstract: Harness-side learning methods such as reflection and prompt evolution let an LLM agent improve from outcome feedback without updating its weights. In finance the natural feedback is a market or policy outcome, and such an outcome is a useful reward only when the documents the agent reads carry learnable information about it. We report a verified benchmark for outcome-guided reading of Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) minutes, built on Cieslak and Vissing-Jorgensen's study of the "Fed put," the Federal Reserve's tendency to ease policy after poor stock-market performance. The benchmark contains 1,197 equity-market passages from the minutes of 200 meetings (2000-2024), fixed chronological splits, an audited reconstruction of the authors' automated phrase-and-direction method, and the authors' human-coded tone counts, which we recover from their published figures. Screening two candidate rewards with frozen readers (fixed models and instructions) gives opposite answers. The equity return that preceded a meeting is learnable from the minutes. A frozen embedding recovers it with an out-of-sample R^2 of 0.50, and tone labels from a frozen LLM reach 0.49, against 0.32 for a linear readout of the reconstructed phrase-and-direction counts. The next change in the policy rate shows no detectable signal. In a test specified before estimation, no text representation beats a baseline without text. A pilot with a frozen LLM reader exposes a credit-assignment problem. One crisis meeting accounts for 79% of the pilot's feedback error, although the reader labels all of its passages negative, the correct direction. An LLM reflector that rewrites the reader's instructions from outcome residuals would therefore be pushed to change labels whose direction is already right. We release the environment, comparators, and a validation-gated adaptation protocol. We have not yet run the adaptive comparisons.

detail.abstract: We study how presidential seniority relates to U.S. stock returns from 1945 to 2024. Value-weighted returns are concave in months in office, and the pattern survives term-clustered and wild-bootstrap inference, term fixed effects, and election-cycle controls. The concavity comes from the lame-duck year: in the final twelve months of a second term, monthly returns are about 1.4 percentage points lower than in a president's first year. We develop a model in which investors price policy-continuity risk but attend to it only when the transition becomes salient. Consistent with the model, the decline is concentrated in the July-October general-election campaign, returns do not fall in re-election years, and macroeconomic uncertainty rises before open-seat elections and falls after incumbent wins. Investor risk aversion, policy-news uncertainty, sentiment, and approval do not explain the effect. Because it rests on few episodes, we report its sensitivity to 2008 in detail.

detail.abstract: This paper examines whether every mining exploitation licence in Guatemala must invariably be preceded by consultation with Indigenous peoples living near a proposed project. It argues that Mining Law Decree 48-97 does not establish such consultation as a universal licensing requirement and that geographical proximity alone does not demonstrate direct impact. Using doctrinal, textual and case-law analysis, the research assesses the domestic mining framework, International Labour Organization Convention No. 169, and the Constitutional Court judgment in case 4785-2017. Its findings distinguish an international duty to consult when substantive legal conditions are met from the judicial transformation of that duty into an across-the-board administrative prerequisite. The article criticises the latter interpretation on grounds of legality, legal certainty, institutional competence and individualised reasoning. It does not deny treaty-based obligations in cases involving demonstrable direct effects on Indigenous peoples; rather, it rejects automatic application to every mining licence without a fact-specific assessment.

detail.abstract: Contraceptive health promotion prioritizes information provision and method uptake, yet neither necessarily demonstrates voluntary or achievable choice. This conceptual paper develops a multilevel framework that explains how gender-transformative health promotion may link information to the ability and opportunity to make and enact contraceptive decisions. A purposive synthesis integrates perspectives on gender and power, reproductive autonomy and rights, and the capability approach. The framework links contextual conditions, strategies at the individual, relational, community, and service levels, mechanisms of change, and the quality of contraceptive choice. It proposes five complementary dimensions: informedness, voluntariness, preference alignment, practical feasibility, and revisability. Six theoretical propositions specify mediating relationships, contextual constraints, and the role of opportunities to reconsider decisions. The framework connects access under Sustainable Development Goal target 3.7 with reproductive decision-making and rights under target 5.6, while distinguishing its proposed measures from official indicators. Practical implications include eliciting private preferences, balanced counseling, voluntary partner involvement, accessible follow-up, and evaluation beyond uptake. The framework has not been empirically tested, and its dimensions should not be treated as a validated scale. Future research should clarify conceptual boundaries, assess measurement properties, and examine mechanisms across populations and service settings. Its contribution is an integrated explanation of choice as an ongoing, socially situated process.

detail.abstract: This technical research note establishes an explicit algorithmic roadmap and structural procedure required to compute Moore's R and isolate underlying physical asset returns natively from option cross-sections. Moore’s R is computed by reversing the Black Scholes model and solving for the rate.  Operating under the structural assumption that the Moore framework represents the optimal Fokker-Planck probability envelope for contingent valuation architecture, this paper details the precise mapping rules required to transition between real-world market metrics and internal state-space replication vectors. Left unconstrained, traditional software search routines encounter severe multi-root identity loops and short-term volatility leaks, frequently generating distorted artificial outputs. This note clarifies the necessary implementation guardrails—specifically the step-by-step state-space balance constraints and a unified down-day risk floor—to insulate the computer loop from software distortion. By explicitly retaining contract time value (t) across all equations, the protocol is designed to preserve dimensional consistency and support reproducible implementation. The theoretical derivations and empirical tests supporting the broader Moore framework are developed in the companion studies cited in the references. This document has the narrower purpose of specifying the programming architecture required to assemble and test the automated financial computing workstation.

detail.abstract: This paper studies how firms finance artificial intelligence (AI). We combine a firm-year measure of AI intensity with Compustat balance sheets and DealScan syndicated loan contracts. Alongside reduced-form within-firm regressions, we use two identification designs: a shift-share instrument built from AI diffusion within a firm's industry, and a stacked difference-in-differences design around the year a firm first reaches the AI frontier. We find that as firms become more AI-intensive, they (i) hold less cash and borrow more, (ii) move from revolving credit into term loans, (iii) pay higher interest spreads and pledge more receivables, inventory, and intangibles, (iv) borrow more under earnings-based covenants, and (v) raise more institutional credit, especially from non-bank lenders. Both designs confirm these responses, which accompany an expansion in investment, employment, and profitability. AI adoption thus tends to replace liquidity buffers with drawn and  earnings-contingent debt that is increasingly held outside the banking system.

detail.abstract: Risk sharing is typically estimated using models that rely on both tails of the incomegrowth distribution, yet agents care more about downside risks. We focus on negative income shocks, developing a methodology to estimate channels of downside-risk sharing and extend it to increasingly severe shocks-an issue important to policymakers but overlooked in prior work. We find that federal transfers and taxes absorb a large share of income-growth fluctuations, a result earlier studies understated. title: The European Dimension Of Spatial Planning

detail.title: The European Dimension Of Spatial Planning

detail.abstract: Spatial planning remains institutionally embedded in national, regional and local legal orders, but the substantive freedom of planning authorities has been progressively reconfigured by European Union law. The Union does not possess an undifferentiated competence to prescribe national land-use plans. Nevertheless, Treaty provisions on territorial cohesion and environmental protection, strategic environmental assessment, nature conservation, water policy, transport and energy networks, maritime spatial planning and Union financing collectively exert an extensive influence on the distribution of activities in space. This study identifies the legal mechanisms through which European norms shape planning decisions, distinguishes binding requirements from intergovernmental agendas and policy coordination, and examines the increasing significance of scientific assessment, public participation, alternatives, judicial review and climate adaptation. It argues that the European dimension of spatial planning is best understood as a plural legal architecture of constraints, procedures, objectives and incentives rather than as a uniform supranational land-use code. Particular attention is devoted to the Court of Justice's case law and to the tensions between renewable deployment, biodiversity protection, infrastructure development and territorial equity.

detail.abstract: Courts in the United States have begun to decide whether training AI systems on copyrighted works can be fair use, but early decisions diverge and turn on narrow records. This paper organizes the relevant questions along a four-stage chain (data, training, output, market) and uses three decisions, Thomson Reuters v. Ross Intelligence, Bartz v. Anthropic, and Kadrey v. Meta Platforms, to identify questions that courts have treated as material: competition and market evidence, source and manner of acquisition, and the proof required for market harm. It then proposes Runtime Legitimacy as an analytical and evidentiary framework under which the legitimacy of data use is supported by use-specific, version-linked, and reassessable records, and states three hypotheses and one normative proposition. The paper compares the proposal with the EU AI Act and the Directive on copyright in the Digital Single Market, examines how Iranian copyright, software, and electronic-commerce texts may bear on the questions, and describes implementation through contracts, record architecture, and professional standards. The framework is a proposal, not existing doctrine, and the propositions are offered for testing.

detail.abstract: This paper separates three design problems that are often bundled together in pay-as-you-go (PAYG) reform: the financing base, compensation of cohorts that lose at the transition, and prospective fertility policy. In a two-period overlapping-generations (OLG) economy with endogenous fertility, saving, and capital accumulation, population decline concentrates pension finance on a shrinking wage-tax base. A permanent shift toward consumption-tax finance broadens the base to retirees but makes current retirees transition losers. A minimum lump-sum transfer neutralizes this political loss, and partial debt finance of the transfer creates a nonempty all-modeled-cohort non-loss region in the log benchmark; the welfare slack is quantitatively thin but the existence result survives the reported constant relative risk aversion (CRRA) curvature exercises. We then compare child allowances and fertility-linked pensions after the tax-base transition. At given prices they can generate identical private fertility support, yet payment timing changes saving, capital accumulation, transition compensation, PAYG liabilities, and cohort welfare. Equal gross policy-outlay comparisons show that instrument rankings depend on the implementation criterion, policy scale, and preference curvature. The quantitative mechanism is scale dependent: as policy intensity changes, the binding implementation constraint can switch from the reform-date worker to a future worker cohort. The policy that is easiest to implement politically therefore need not be the policy that best protects current and future cohorts while raising fertility.

detail.abstract: Sterling-denominated stablecoins remain a small and insufficiently documented segment of the digital asset market. Inconsistent public data, diverse issuance arrangements, and uncertainty about transaction activity complicate their assessment. This study examines six British pound stablecoins across five blockchains using blockchain explorers, official issuer documentation, third-party listings, and daily market data covering approximately one year. First, the combined market capitalization of the six tokens was approximately 30 million United States dollars, about 0.01 percent of the dollar stablecoin market. Second, the tokens follow four distinct issuance models with differing consumer protection, and neither of the two UK-based issuers offers deposit-compensation coverage. Third, supply and ownership were highly concentrated, with one token representing approximately 87 percent of the market, and transfer counts did not reliably indicate payment use: some activity was consistent with automated trading, while 78 percent of one token's transactions over twelve months were card payments made by a small but recurring group of users whose activity declined during the period. Conflicting public figures and issuer information further demonstrated the need for independent verification. These findings inform the assessment of market maturity, consumer protection, and transparency in the British pound stablecoin ecosystem and the wider debate on a digital pound.

detail.abstract: Cross-dataset generalization and deployment cost are two largely independent obstacles to the clinical translation of polyp segmentation. We present WaveLite-DG, a compact encoder–decoder addressing both. It combines a MobileNetV3-Large encoder, Wavelet Frequency Modules that perturb approximation-band feature statistics during training while enhancing detail-band structure, a gated context scan at the bottleneck, and a boundary-supervised decoder. We derive in closed form the energy this perturbation injects. Trained on Kvasir-SEG and CVC-ClinicDB, with CVC-ColonDB, ETIS-LaribPolypDB and CVC-300 withheld from every fitting and selection decision, WaveLite-DG reaches a three-seed mean macro unseen Dice of 0.8300 ± 0.0004, the highest of six architectures retrained under one protocol without photometric augmentation and statistically equivalent to Polyp-PVT and VM-UNet within a pre-set margin of 0.02. With colour jitter, or with the perturbation added to those two baselines, they lead by under 0.008. In every regime tested WaveLite-DG stays within 0.008 of the best model with one third or less of the parameters (7.68 M) and one fifth or less of the computation (1.93 giga multiply–accumulate operations), and it is 0.0427 more accurate than the best of four lightweight networks. Approximation-band perturbation adds +0.0651 macro Dice without photometric augmentation but only +0.0185 with colour jitter, which recovers most of the gain, and perturbing the undecomposed feature at matched energy shows no detectable difference. The contribution therefore lies in efficiency at parity rather than in a new mechanism.

detail.abstract: State sovereign immunity is a complex issue in international law. Removing a legal entity or its property from jurisdictional control undermines the legal principle of accountability and the absence of impunity. As a result, it directly jeopardizes the rule of law. The United Nations Convention of December 2, 2004, on Jurisdictional Immunities of States and Their Property (“UNCJIS”) was adopted to remedy uncertainty in the field. In Tran To Nga v. Dow Chemical et al. (hereinafter “the French Agent Orange case”),[x] the Paris Court of Appeal failed to apply the UNCJIS guidelines and rendered a decision contrary to customary international law.[xi] This case illustrates the dangers to the rule of law and human rights posed by judges who do not follow the provisions of the UNCJIS. The precedent set by the Paris Court of Appeal’s decision would have devastating legal consequences if affirmed. In relation to human rights violations, this would mean that any activity by any non-state actor is protected worldwide beyond a state’s jurisdiction, as long as it is a contractor of that state.Part I of this Article presents the Paris Court’s decision. It shows the decision’s weak reasoning and raises concerns regarding the court’s impartiality. Part II discusses how customary international law runs counter to the court’s decision: international jurisdictional immunity does not extend to mere[xxii] state contractors, especially in cases of serious human rights abuse. Part III examines how the UNCJIS is relevant worldwide as a codification of customary law and addresses the absence of immunity for state contractors. Part IV shows how the ECHR mandates states not to provide additional immunity beyond that prescribed by international law, and that the UNCJIS binds France under the European Court of Human Rights’ (“ECtHR”) case law. Part V rejects the doctrine of forum non conveniens. The Article concludes that the UNCJIS is a decisive tool for avoiding legal errors, biases, and perceptions of bias. It is therefore a crucial tool to bind judges in ECHR jurisdictions, thus benefiting the rule of law worldwide.

detail.abstract: Many countries smooth fuel prices with a formula and a stabilisation fund. This paper asks whether Mauritius follows its formula, what departures from it cost, and whether a better rule exists. A record of 84 pricing reviews (168 decisions), checked against the regulator's own calculations and price structures, shows that the formula was followed in 90 of 94 verifiable decisions, including 20 of 24 unpopular increases; the exceptions were ministerial vetoes. Politics entered instead through vetoes, six price-setting interventions and levies that absorbed falls in world prices. Oil price spikes since 1987 typically lasted about eight months, and Mauritian consumer prices rose after fuel increases more than they fell after cuts, most clearly bus fares, which never fell. Simulating eight pricing rules on 2011–2026 costs shows that full pass-through minimises fiscal cost but allows six-month price rises of 44–89%, while actual practice was smooth only by leaving up to Rs 6.6 billion (petrol) and Rs 9.7 billion (diesel) of cost unrecovered. A modified Mauritian rule, with a six-month trend reference, 5% steps, a fund borrowing limit and reserve rebuilding, cuts the largest six-month rise to 28–34% at a fiscal exposure close to the current rule's, and does so again over 2019–2026. In a loss function that weighs price volatility, reversed increases and fiscal exposure, it ranks first whenever fiscal exposure carries between about 30% and 60% of the weight.

detail.abstract: We develop a tractable asset-pricing model in which risk- and ambiguity-averse investors hold heterogeneous beliefs about future fundamental values. Greater belief dispersion may increase ambiguity because investors become less confident that any particular belief is correct. The closed-form solution demonstrates that expected returns increase with belief dispersion because investors require an additional premium to bear ambiguity arising from heterogeneous beliefs. The model also predicts that belief dispersion increases volatility and has an inverse U-shaped effect on trading volume. Our model suggests that belief dispersion may serve as a priced factor by linking heterogeneous beliefs to ambiguity.

detail.abstract: This paper proposes a monetary policy rule designed to stabilize inflation that follows a law of motion analogous to Newtonian mechanics. In response to inflationary pressures, the central bank raises the nominal interest rate. However, this policy intervention inevitably induces disutility for households, which is proportional to the "kinetic energy." Crucially, there exists a per-period upper bound on the disutility acceptable to households. This paper demonstrates that inflation can ultimately be stabilized under the constraint that the central bank implements stabilization measures while keeping disutility below this threshold. Furthermore, this policy implementation is shown to be consistent with the Taylor rule.

detail.abstract: A consumption bundle compresses a consumption process, including its order and intermediate history, into final quantities. We characterize Bundle Sufficiency under standard rationality by Zero-Quantity Neutrality, Within-Good Adjacent Aggregation, and Adjacent Exchange Invariance. The main economic results concern identification. When consumers can freely optimize over sequences within a bundle and cost depends only on final quantities, primitive plan preferences affect ordinary quantity behavior only through the induced bundle preference obtained after within-bundle sequence optimization. The full primitive ordering over plans therefore cannot generally be recovered from quantity behavior. Under standard conditions, the resulting quantity projection is consistent with GARP and ordinary Afriat rationalization. Moreover, a continuum of continuous, regular primitive preferences can generate the same baseline bundle demand and the same optimally chosen baseline sequence while producing different counterfactual demand and compensating variation under a closed sequence restriction. Finally, a fixed-bundle three-good designed-menu benchmark shows how otherwise unchosen sequence alternatives can be placed on the choice margin to identify hidden pairwise order signs.

detail.abstract: This article advances the concept of discriminatory corruption, the use of public authority to exploit or reinforce social hierarchies of exclusion, to explain how corruption and institutionalized homophobia interact within political systems. While prior studies have noted that marginalized groups face unique vulnerabilities to corruption, this study theorizes the institutional processes that link legal discrimination, weak accountability, and social exclusion. It identifies two pathways: coercive corruption, where officials exploit discriminatory laws for personal or political gain, and institutional corruption, where systemic prejudice erodes oversight and normalizes impunity. Drawing on cross-national data from over 150 countries, the analysis uses instrumental-variable regression and structural equation modelling to estimate how corruption, democracy, and legal discrimination relate to LGBTQI+ acceptance. The results indicate that corruption consistently suppresses social and legal inclusion, even in democratic contexts, and that criminalizing laws amplify these effects. By integrating human rights and governance literatures, the article reframes corruption as an informal institution that reproduces identity-based inequality, expanding the study of accountability and representation in comparative politics.

detail.abstract: Can shared experiences across nations foster people's attachment to a community beyond the nation-state? The answer is a priori ambiguous: international events bring nations together around a common frame, but they also set them against one another. To answer this question, we study the Eurovision Song Contest, an annual competition broadcast to a large transnational audience and organized around shared European values. Comparing respondents surveyed just before and after their country's participation in the show, we find that the contest raises European identification, which complements national identity rather than substituting for it. The effect persists over time and is independent of the outcome of the event. Regarding mechanisms, we show that Eurovision changes the values individuals attribute to Europe without changing their own values, and identification increases when the two align. Importantly, the event has electoral consequences: in countries that narrowly qualify for the final, votes in European Parliament elections shift toward more pro-European parties.

detail.abstract: The rapid growth of music streaming has changed how musical popularity is discovered, measured, and sustained. While viral exposure can generate substantial short-term increases in streaming activity, the extent to which songs retain audience attention after reaching peak popularity remains less clearly defined. This study introduces the Viral Longevity Index (VLI), a quantitative measure designed to evaluate post-viral streaming retention relative to a song's identified peak. The study analyzes a purposive sample of 30 songs representing different artists, genres, release periods, and pathways to viral popularity. Historical Spotify streaming and chart data were used to identify viral entry, peak streaming activity, and post-peak streaming levels at 30, 90, and 180 days. The VLI combines these three retention measures using weighted contributions of 30%, 30%, and 40%, respectively, with greater weight assigned to longer-term retention. Based on VLI scores, songs were classified into four post-viral trajectory types: Flash Viral, Short-Lived Viral, Sustained Viral, and Long-Tail. The results demonstrate substantial variation in post-viral streaming trajectories. VLI scores ranged from 2.8% to 78.9%, indicating considerable differences in the extent to which songs retained streaming activity following their viral peaks. Exploratory analysis also identified strong relationships between VLI and longerterm retention and chart persistence. These findings suggest that viral popularity and post-viral longevity represent distinct dimensions of streaming performance. The VLI provides a standardized framework for examining this distinction and offers a quantitative approach to studying the durability of viral music success.

detail.abstract: Financial-services AI governance often relies on disclosing artificial intelligence (AI) involvement, yet it is unclear whether customers identify who made the decision. In a 3 × 2 vignette experiment on a partially approved insurance claim, 402 respondents were randomly assigned to a disclosed decision authority (officer decides on an AI recommendation; AI decides with brief officer review; AI decides alone) and to a lower-or higher-impact scenario. Only 39.8% chose the answer matching the disclosure. "AI with human review" was the most common answer in every condition. Under condition-invariant default responses, a post hoc threshold-with-guessing model estimated a disclosure-consistent component of .14 (95% CI .07-.21). Partial identification shows that its size, and even its positivity, depends on how far defaults differ across conditions. Disclosed authority had no detectable average effect on procedural fairness. The higher-impact scenario package lowered fairness. As hypothesised, lower fairness was associated with higher escalation preference. The study separates disclosed from attributed decision authority. Under stated assumptions, it shows how far manipulationcheck match rates can reflect default responding. Insurers and regulators may want to test whether customers identify AI authority after disclosure.

detail.abstract: This quantitative correlational study evaluated the level of internet accessibility and the extent of GCash payment adoption among 134 registered micro-entrepreneurs in Barangays Anislagan, San Roque, and San Juan, Maco, Davao de Oro. Primary data collected via a validated survey instrument revealed that internet accessibility scored a moderate composite mean (2.97 out of 5.00), with signal stability during business hours scoring significantly lower (2.87 out of 5.00). Overall GCash payment adoption remained low (1.85 out of 5.00), with 38.8 percent of micro-merchants operating completely outside the e-wallet ecosystem. detail.abstract: PurposeThis study asks how suspicion is produced, circulated and settled in platform-mediated marketplaces when price becomes the most legible signal of trustworthiness. It moves the study of consumer suspicion beyond the buyer’s evaluation of a message or a review towards suspicion as a market-level condition that buyers, sellers, platforms and state agencies jointly sustain.Design/methodology/approachThe study analyses a corpus of 1,821 verbatim units of naturally occurring public discourse about Indonesian marketplaces (2023–2026), drawn from 250 public pages and 25 publishers and voiced by 776 identifiable speakers: consumer complaint letters and their comment threads, sellers’ open letters, and named statements by officials, associations and platform spokespersons. A theoretical sampling pool of 539 dense units from the two focal layers — consumers and sellers, treated as equal rather than as principal and foil — was coded following the Gioia methodology into 68 first-order concepts, 29 second-order themes and seven aggregate dimensions, supported by a cross-layer lexical comparison and a stratified verification audit.FindingsParticipants treat an unreasonably low price as a diagnostic instrument and as a moral ledger. As platform-issued signals (badges, authenticity labels, seals, ratings) lose guaranteeing power, price substitutes for them, and verification becomes unpaid private labour on both sides of the transaction: buyers film unboxings, sellers film packing. Guarantees sold in advance convert, at the moment of dispute, into evidentiary tests whose criteria are withheld; meanwhile the platform’s automated systems suspect buyers (“unusual activity”) and sellers (“suspicious transactions”, “fake orders”) alike. The authors theorise this configuration as distributed suspicion, operating through two mechanisms: the privatisation of proof and the constitution of price as a vernacular institution.

detail.abstract: Video platforms monetize content supplied by independent creators, and comment sections are where audiences address creators in their own words. Do comments steer what creators produce next? We study 291 knowledge creators on Bilibili, a Chinese video platform, over 2024. An LLM-assisted classifier labels the most-liked comments on 24,243 videos by focus (creator or content) and contribution (constructive suggestions or ideas); its agreement with independent human coding is fair to moderate. Comparing videos of the same creator, we relate comment composition to the following week’s output, correct for measurement error in the shares with split-half instrumental variables, and judge estimates against a ±5% equivalence bound fixed before any corrected estimate was computed. As measured by the classifier, content-focused and constructive comments are not followed by meaningful changes in the number or like rate of subsequent videos: all eight pre-specified estimates are equivalent to zero within ±5% per 10-point rise in a share, and within ±2% for constructive comments. Feedback intervention theory predicts lower like rates after creator-focused comments; declines beyond about 1% can be ruled out, though rises of up to about 7–8% cannot. For creator-focused comments and posting, the negative association among typical creators is matched by a placebo using comments written after the outcome window, so it cannot be attributed to comments. Large between-creator associations, which would suggest that comments matter, depend on a few prolific creators and on controls. For platforms, comment composition is not a demonstrated lever on creator supply.

detail.abstract: How does AI acceleration change softwware engineering in public policy? Thiis paper argues that developers' responsibilities increasingly concern architecture, including the organizational arrangements governing consequential technical decisions. Drawing on practitioner accounts and organizational scholarship, it examines a conditional mechanism: implementation may accelerate faster than participants discover and reconcile diffeering assumptions. Thiose assumptions acquire technical consequences, while implementation changes expectations, relationships, and subsequent requirements. title: PAPER 05 - The Execution Surface: Why Distributed Compute Cannot Be Shared

detail.title: PAPER 05 - The Execution Surface: Why Distributed Compute Cannot Be Shared

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None declared. The author is an independent researcher; this work was self-funded, with no external funding, institutional affiliation, or organizational relationship influencing it.

detail.abstract:
Compute is moving outward. That argument is over, and this paper does not make it. It starts from the condition itself and asks what kind of thing is being built. The answer is a planetary execution surface: a continuous layer of local compute running from gigawatt campuses down to milliwatt endpoints, thickest wherever consequences occur. It is being assembled now, segment by segment, by thousands of unrelated parties — municipalities meeting statutory duties, retailers avoiding bandwidth costs, manufacturers preventing downtime, remote operators with no alternative, and professionals who cannot send confidential work to somebody else's model.

Four findings follow from describing it rather than arguing for it. First, nobody deploys any of this hardware in order to sell compute. Every box is paid for by a cost avoided or an obligation met, so the capital isn't speculative, and the surface cannot crash the way the fiber build-out did. Spare capacity is a byproduct, and there is an enormous amount of it, because every node's owner sizes for their own peak and peaks are brief.

Second, distributed execution does not fail — markets for distributed execution fail. A decade of well-funded attempts splits on one question: did the arrangement require somebody to rely on work done inside a stranger's machine? Every failure did. Every success had a single owner holding both the hardware and the workload.

Third, two experiments have already tested this at scale, from opposite directions. Carrier edge computing had the best-sited facilities, trusted operators, no counterparty risk, and no market formed. Decentralized compute marketplaces had auctions, enormous supply and discounts of fifty to eighty percent, and production work stayed away. Each diagnosed a different missing piece, and each built it. Neither could tell a buyer what had happened inside the machine.

Fourth, the surface becomes a mesh only when three layers are present — the three the earlier papers in this series derived independently. People compile policy upstream. A deterministic Executable Governance Kernel sits at the boundary. An independent witness runs alongside it. The relationship between the last two is specific and easy to invert: the kernel decides whether an action may proceed, the witness records what it can observe, and the witness never gates anything. Without all three, density is not connection, and what remains is a very large number of capable machines each serving one party.

The paper stops at that gap. The companion paper on machine economics addresses what closing it would be worth, how such capacity would be priced, and whether a market for it would clear.

detail.abstract: AI-based-text chatbots are increasingly embedded in e-commerce, making it important to understand consumer resistance and usage intentions. This study proposes an integrated behavioural framework combining the Technology Acceptance Model, Innovation Resistance Theory, and inertia, with the Throughput Model serving as the organising framework. Using data from 801 UK consumers who had previously interacted with AI text-based chatbots on e-commerce platforms and Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM), findings show that perceived usefulness enhances usage intentions and reduces inertia, while usage, risk, and tradition barriers increase inertia. Inertia is associated with greater resistance and lower usage intentions. Empathy attenuates the negative relationship between inertia and usage intentions, while individual-level collectivism–individualism moderates this relationship. These findings contribute to understanding consumer resistance and adoption of AI-based-text chatbots and offer practical implications for designing e-commerce chatbot experiences that enhance perceived usefulness, address resistance barriers, and reduce inertia.

detail.abstract: Language models can check a policy document against a governance framework one requirement at a time. We ask whether to run one model or several, and whether long documents must be read in pieces. In a small-scale study, four models assessed China's Personal Information Protection Law (15 pages) and Malaysia's Personal Data Protection Act (100 pages) against the 50 core elements of the Health Data Governance Principles in six areas of law, 300 cells each. Two human coders, who were not told what any model had concluded, checked 60 cells per law, weighted back to all cells. The models' misses were shared and their extra findings were individual. Had the four missed evidence independently, together they would have missed about 1% of the evidence in China's law; they missed 22%, against 23% for the most thorough model alone. Cells that only one model flagged held evidence 4 times in 26; cells all four flagged held it 18 times in 19. More models thus added little evidence to a thorough model, but a strong signal of which findings to trust; added to a more cautious model, the others raised recall by 10 to 27 points. Two runs of the same model disagreed on about 30% of the cells either flagged, against about 45% for two different models. On the longer law no loss of recall was visible and wrong findings did not become more frequent, because each cell asks for one qualifying provision, not a complete list; misses and errors concerned which element or area of law a passage serves, not unread pages. The study supports using several models as a cross-check, not as a substitute for judgment: their greatest value is helping people decide what to trust provisionally, what to question, and where to look more closely.

title: Countering Epistemic Centralisation in Frontier AI: Towards Hermeneutical Justice

detail.abstract:
"Epistemic centralisation" is a consequence of building Large Language Models on pre-training datasets that disproportionately represent global knowledge sources. An emerging body of research is revealing the extent to which the design of these Frontier AI models is leading towards what has been called "generative hermeneutical erasure", favouring the "default speaker", a "voice from nowhere". In turn, this is prompting the formation of regional networks committed to equitable language representation and representative training datasets. The global reach of a small set of commercially driven AI platforms is also pushing nations towards "Sovereign AI", although recent surveys show that most sovereign projects depend on partnerships with a small set of US-based Big Tech companies. These trends indicate that creating regional or focused networks to address epistemic centralisation does not, in itself, ensure epistemic justice. As with all technologies, social, economic, and political factors have a determining role, expressing forms of power, grounded in the history of colonialism, that persist long after formal colonial administrations have ended.

The systemic injustices of epistemic centralisation have significant implications for the recording of academic achievement, particularly for the value of credentials recognised and exchanged across national borders, the focus of the Groningen Declaration Network. Ensuring hermeneutical justice in credentialing starts with quality assurance; the benchmarks and standards which underpin trust in teaching and learning. New benchmarks should acknowledge that Artificial Intelligence will soon be ambient, and that assessment must measure the ability to use AI appropriately and critically. The GDN is well positioned to contribute towards these goals through secure forms of digital credentialing and Comprehensive Learner Records, helping create a network of networks that recognises epistemic validity across national borders and global regions.

detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of online food delivery platforms has raised concerns about declining sales at traditional offline retailers. This concern is particularly relevant for convenience stores, which compete with food delivery services for consumers' immediate meal needs. However, food delivery may reshape consumer shopping routines, creating complementary demand for nearby offline retailers. As these forces may operate simultaneously, it remains unclear whether food delivery ultimately benefits or harms convenience stores. Understanding this relationship is important not only for retailers adapting to digital competition but also for assessing how digital platform expansion reshapes consumer behavior and economic activity beyond the platform ecosystem. In collaboration with a service platform in China, we assembled a comprehensive panel dataset of monthly transactions across dozens of product categories for 54 convenience stores. We merged this with restaurant listing data from China's largest food delivery platform. Leveraging a two-way fixed effects model alongside an instrumental variable strategy, we estimate the causal effect of local delivery market density on store performance. We find that a 100-restaurant increase in local food delivery density increases convenience store sales by approximately 6%. We attribute this lift to two primary mechanisms. The first is an inventory-depletion mechanism: as food delivery shifts main meal consumption online, households reduce their bulk grocery trips to supermarkets, thereby increasing their reliance on nearby convenience stores for frequent top-up purchases. The second is a meal-completion mechanism, where delivered meals stimulate immediate demand for complementary add-on items purchased offline. Our findings offer actionable insights for both convenience retailers and food delivery platforms. Businesses can capture delivery-driven spillovers by strategically emphasizing complementary add-on items, tailoring assortments to consumers' needs in residential and commercial neighborhoods, and designing local partnerships that seamlessly coordinate online meal delivery with nearby offline top-up purchases.

detail.abstract: The proliferation of autonomous multi-agent systems necessitates a fundamental departure from strictly technical frameworks of artificial intelligence alignment. This paper integrates Anthony Giddens' structuration theory with Bruno Latour's actor-network theory to conceptualize machine agents not as emergent sentiences but as non-human actants bearing the inscribed normative delegations of human institutions. When these sociotechnical networks are prematurely sealed from scrutiny, they precipitate the administrative catastrophe Hannah Arendt termed the rule by Nobody. By conflating procedural cognition with reflexive moral thought, algorithmic governance risks substituting technical fabrication for authentic political action. Drawing upon Karl Popper's defense of the open society, this work argues that preserving democratic legitimacy in the age of recursive machine learning requires defending the Arendtian space of appearance. Institutions must maintain structures of human accountability that actively resist the diffusion of moral responsibility across opaque algorithmic pipelines.

detail.abstract: This article examines a deliberative mini-public convened to explore Indigenous cultural competency (ICC) in Australian legal education. Bringing together Indigenous and non-Indigenous legal academics, the initiative sought to develop recommendations for improving ICC pedagogy and strengthening Indigenous participation in legal education. The article situates the experiment within deliberative democratic theory, assessing its design and implementation against principles of inclusion, demographic and ideological diversity, facilitation, and reason-giving. detail.abstract: Every crosscountry ranking of development rests on a denominator chosen by convention. Africa is ranked on output per person, yet its countries organize production across territories that are vast, sparsely built, and unevenly settled. This paper shows that GDP per capita can be written exactly as the product of three observable quantities: output per square kilometre of built-up land, the built-up share of national territory, and territory per person. The Africa-non-Africa gap in GDP per capita therefore splits exactly into a gap in the productivity of developed space, a gap in settlement extent, and a gap in territorial endowment, each computable from public satellite-derived data in the Global Human Settlement Layer. The decomposition yields a first test that requires no regression: if territorial extent shapes Africa's measured performance, its gap must be materially smaller on output per unit of built-up land than on output per unit of total land. We embed settlement intensity in a knowledge-augmented, AIgeneralized growth model, derive its level and growth implications, and pre-specify the estimators, sensitivity ranges, and a nine-item falsification scorecard before any data are analysed. The design places three rival explanations of the measured gap in a single framework, namely how countries are represented on maps, how their territory is physically settled, and how their output is statistically measured, and exploits the fact that built-up land, being observed from space, is immune to the survey weaknesses that affect national accounts.

detail.abstract: A purely mathematical document integrity system must allow an author to irrevocably bind the semantic content of a text to the visible vector geometry of a seal without relying on centralized verifi cation servers, raster pixel noise, or decorative visual stamps. Conventional digital signatures detach the binary CMS / PKCS#7 (IETF RFC 5652) container from the visual rendering of the page, whereas raster watermarks degrade under scaling and vector conversion. In this paper, we propose the Marma Crypto protocol — a dual-layer cryptographic geometric watermarking system that deterministically maps an elliptic curve digital signature vector (𝑟, 𝑠) over the characteristic-two Galois field GF(2257) per Ukrainian National Standard DSTU 4145-2002 (coupled with GOST 34.311-95, DSTU 7564:2014 “Kupyna”, and FIPS 180-4 SHA-256 message digests) via a 24-bit block quantizer directly into floating point vertex micro-perturbations 𝛿𝑘 ∈ [−10−5,+10−5] of the nine interlocking triangles of the classical Sri Yantra (Nava-Cakra). Because the nine triangles are governed by a nonlinear concurrency system of 54 triple intersections (marmas), identically preserve the analytical bilateral symmetry invariant � �𝑥𝑘 +𝑟𝑥𝑘 = 2𝐶𝑥, and encapsulate a long-term ETSI EN 319 142-1 (PAdES-B-LTA) signature container with an RFC 3161 Time-Stamp Token and ISO 32000-2 Document Security Store (/DSS), the resulting vector seal is optically indistinguishable from the canonical geometric archetype while enabling keyless public verification and zero-tolerance detection of any single-byte text modification or vertex drift exceeding 10−7 coordinate units.

detail.abstract: When a constrained optimizer selects a portfolio, managers, auditors and regulators ask why. Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to answer in plain language, but a fluent explanation can cite reasons that did not drive the decision. In a linear program, the effect of every constraint on the optimum is known from the solver's certificate and can be confirmed by relaxing the constraint and resolving. Each claim in an explanation ("this limit drove the allocation and is worth about x basis points") can therefore be checked against ground truth rather than against another model or a human judge. We apply this test to 196 bond-portfolio problems built from public FRED data on US Treasury yields and ICE BofA credit spreads (May to October 2026), scoring explanations written by Claude Sonnet 4.5 and Gemini 2.5 Flash without access to the certificate. Across 149 cases in which a limit had exactly zero effect on the optimum, the models named it as a driver in 89% (Claude) and 77% (Gemini) of cases, while naming binding limits in 98% and 90% of cases. Giving the models the portfolio facts that show which limits are tight left Claude's rate essentially unchanged (86%) and reduced Gemini's to 48%, no better than a fixed template that always names the same two limits (50%). The models' estimates of what each binding limit costs were within ±35% of the true value in 7% of 1,703 claims, with median errors ranging from 0.29× to 8.43× the true value and in the same direction for both vendors, even though the holdings shown to the models determine the true values. A third model, GPT-4o-mini, copied the numbers in the prompt's format example and is reported separately. Explanations generated from the certificate avoid both errors by construction.

detail.abstract: Building Information Modelling (BIM) and digital-twin coordination cut design clashes, rework and change orders in architectural projects. The technical case is well established. The management question is less studied: should an architectural practice build coordination capability in-house, subscribe to a cloud coordination platform, or contract a specialist BIM consultancy? We build a sourcing model. In it, annual net benefit depends on four things: the number of active projects, the avoidable rework cost per project, the loaded cost of design labour, and the effective cost of capital, scaled by a capital-availability index. We apply it to stylized practices in the United States and the United Kingdom. Four results follow. First, below about 6 active projects (US) and 10 (UK), no route pays. Second, a subscription platform is best for small portfolios, and a contracted consultancy for medium ones. Third, in-house capability leads every other route only above about 45 projects in the US and 44 in the UK. Fourth, unlike in capital-constrained economies, the UK in-house threshold responds much more to labour cost than to capital access. Raising UK design wages to US levels would push it from about 44 to about 63 projects. Raising UK capital access to the US level would lower it only to about 39. In these high-income economies, the binding constraint on design self-reliance therefore appears to be skilled labour, not capital.

detail.abstract: As AI voice agents get deployed in high-volume contact centers, firms can route low-intent leads to AI and allocate high-intent leads to human workers. Drawing on sequential search theory, we posit that AI-induced task allocation reshapes work, enriching opportunities facing human workers but also raising their reservation value for continuing with the lead in hand, making them less willing to persist. We study the effects of an AI voice-agent deployment at a Chinese online health-insurance brokerage using more than a half million customer outreach records surrounding the rollout. Adopting a regression-discontinuity-in-time design, we trace how worker behavior changes across the workday. Results show that the enrichment of human-facing opportunities concentrates early in the workday, raising the probability that a call is a high-intent lead by about 23 percentage points on the first three calls and fading to zero later. However, customer acquisition by human workers declines precisely where the enrichment is greatest, falling about 5 percentage points on the first three calls and flattening over the day. Consistent with the theorized reservation value mechanism, workers reallocate their earliest leads about 8 percentage points more often and persist less with them, shortening those calls by about 13%. A calibrated decomposition analysis further shows that the modest gain from improved lead ordering is outweighed by a much larger negative behavioral response. By reshaping the quality and within-workday distribution of opportunities, parallel AI deployment alters how workers pursue tasks, highlighting opportunity distribution as an important service operations state variable beyond workload and congestion.
