detail.abstract: Given the rising significance attributed to the opening up of the strategy processes and practices, along with the acknowledged role that emerging information technologies (IT) can play in supporting open strategizing, this short piece of work aims at understanding the state-of-the-art of research on artificial intelligence (AI) and open strategy, as well as the potential directions for future research. To this aim, the existing pertinent literature is located, and a scoping literature review is conducted in this short study. Our findings provide some initial insights into what has been done so far and what could be done in the next steps of the research on AI and open strategy. Our main contribution is to respond to the growing discourses on the potential integration of this disruptive technology and open strategy work, as well as to lay an initial foundation for bridging the gap that exists in our current understanding of this research landscape's breadth, nature, and range.

detail.abstract: This study examines whether the September 2022 Niemann–Carlsen cheating scandal was associated with measurable shifts in global public search interest in chess. Drawing on Agenda Setting Theory, a Google Trends before-after comparison design was applied across four search terms — chess, chess cheating, Hans Niemann, and Magnus Carlsen — covering a 61-month period (December 2018–December 2023). Results show that overall chess search interest increased by 55.2% following the scandal (p = 0.0007, Cohen's d = 2.160), while scandal-specific terms rose dramatically from near-zero pre-scandal baselines — a pattern reflecting prior absence of search activity rather than an absolute surge in broader chess interest. The increase proved largely persistent for three of the four search terms, with post-scandal confidence intervals excluding pre-scandal means. The peak search interest associated with the scandal (59) approached but did not exceed the peak observed during the 2020 Netflix release of The Queen's Gambit (68). These findings extend Agenda Setting Theory into a novel context, providing empirical evidence that high-profile controversies can elevate topic salience in niche sport communities with low pre-existing mainstream awareness. The study contributes methodologically by demonstrating the viability of Google Trends as a behavioral data source within sport communication research.

detail.abstract:
Background: Health systems increasingly require doctors to contribute not only through clinical care but also through leadership, management, and evidence-informed practice. Although management and research competencies are increasingly recognised as important components of workforce preparedness, their integration into undergraduate medical curricula remains limited. The extent to which doctors are willing to trade clinical training time for these competencies is poorly understood. This study estimated doctors' willingness to give up clinical training time (WTGUT) for management and research competencies in Southern Africa and explored preferences for curriculum design.

Methods: A discrete choice experiment was conducted among doctors in Southern Africa. Attributes and levels were informed by prior qualitative research and pilot studies conducted between 2021 and 2023. Preferences for trade-offs between clinical, management, and research training were analysed using a conditional logit model with a non-linear specification of clinical training time. Preference heterogeneity was explored using the Resistance to Change-Beliefs scale.

Findings: A total of 203 doctors completed the survey, of whom 190 provided sufficient data for analysis. Most respondents worked primarily in clinical settings (58·9%; 112/190). Participants were willing to trade 4·46 hours of clinical training per week for management competencies and 4·38 hours for research competencies. The strongest preferences were for competencies related to managing self and others, and using research evidence in practice. Respondents with stronger preferences for tradition were less willing to trade clinical training time for management and research content.

Interpretation: Doctors in Southern Africa were willing to trade substantial clinical training time for management and research competencies, supporting a broader conception of workforce preparedness beyond clinical expertise alone. Preferences were strongest for competencies related to managing self and others and applying research evidence in practice, suggesting that these capabilities are viewed as complementary to clinical training. Integrating management and research competencies into undergraduate medical education may help align curricula with evolving workforce and health-system needs.

detail.abstract: This paper revisits the linear adaptive bus holding control framework with three modifications. First, we replace its deterministic dwell-time model with a more realistic M/G/1 boarding process in which passengers who arrive during dwelling can also board. Second, we shift control decisions from bus arrival times to ready-to-depart (RTD) times, the moment boarding is complete, so the control law uses the realized dwell time instead of predicting it. Third, we apply a nonlinear ramp function that keeps the computed holding time nonnegative, so the slack no longer has to be large to guarantee nonnegativity and instead becomes a free tuning parameter. The resulting control subsumes the classical adaptive controls in the literature as special cases. We prove finite-horizon probabilistic stability of the nonlinear RTD-based Simple Control under the coupled M/G/1 boarding model. We derive an explicit slack condition for this stability guarantee. We test these modifications in simulation on both an idealized homogeneous route and a route calibrated to bus line No. 8 in Chengdu, China. Our proposed nonlinear RTD control outperforms both the conventional linear arrival-based control and carefully tuned reinforcement learning agents, the latter even on the headway objective they are trained for. Within our nonlinear RTD framework, traditional schedule-based holding is generally Pareto efficient for schedule adherence despite using no real-time headway information. This contradicts the long-standing view that it is inferior to adaptive control. Therefore, we argue that the proposed nonlinear RTD-based holding controls, despite their simplicity, suffice for effective single-line bunching mitigation.

detail.abstract: Valued everyday consumption may remain unstable under constrained routines. Using Gen Z breakfast-option adoption as an empirical case, this sequential and complementary multi-study design examined the breakfast value-adoption gap. Study 1 mapped 44,823 social media comments, Study 2 contextualised the identified patterns through 21 interviews, and Study 3 analysed 1,949 offline survey responses using a contextualised stimulus-organism-response model. Time pressure and access friction were positively associated with perceived negative affect and four value-appraisal dimensions. Perceived negative affect was positively associated with all four dimensions, which were positively associated with adoption intention. These 2 associations remained stable across supplementary analyses. Importance-performance analysis identified routine-fit and emotional value appraisal as higher improvement priorities than functional value, informing routine-compatible breakfast-option design in constrained mornings.

detail.abstract: The division of labor is fundamental to how firms organize production. Since Adam Smith, economists have recognized that dividing tasks more finely increases productivity through specialization but also raises coordination costs-a tradeoff formalized by Becker and Murphy (1992). Yet we have little systematic evidence on how this tradeoff operates within firms. Moreover, this classical perspective overlooks a second, dynamic tradeoff: firms not only produce output, but also develop a central input into future production-their workers' human capital. A finer division of labor allows workers to develop greater expertise through repeated performance of narrowly defined tasks, but may also reduce opportunities to learn from coworkers by limiting interactions and knowledge exchange. We study both tradeoffs using population-wide Norwegian employer-employee records, linked workplace surveys, quasi-experimental variation in coworker availability, and randomized experiments with workers and managers. We find that more specialized firms exhibit higher productivity but also greater coordination costs. Their workers report more learning-by-doing but substantially less coworker learning, resulting in lower overall learning and slower wage growth. To establish the importance of coworker learning for human capital accumulation, we exploit extended coworker absences and show that losing access to colleagues reduces subsequent wage growth, particularly in occupations characterized by greater task overlap and coworker learning. To isolate the role of the division of labor from other workplace characteristics, we conduct randomized experiments that vary task allocation in otherwise identical workplaces. Workers and managers anticipate greater coordination demands, weaker coworker interactions, and lower skill accumulation under greater specialization. The experiments then ask workers to choose their preferred workplace and managers how they would organize production. Both favor greater task overlap, citing coworker interactions and learning opportunities as key reasons for their choices. Together, our findings show that the division of labor shapes not only the efficiency of current production but also the accumulation of human capital and future productive capacity.

detail.abstract: Rural products crafted by indigenous communities represent a significant cultural heritage and economic livelihood. However, marketing these products beyond traditional localized boundaries remains a persistent challenge. This paper empirically investigates the key problems and future prospects of marketing tribal and rural products originating from the tribal regions of Odisha, India. A structured empirical study was conducted across major tribaldominated districts of Odisha, including Mayurbhanj, Koraput, and Kandhamal, to investigate key marketing bottlenecks and identify the primary determinants of sales performance among tribal producers. Primary data were collected from a representative sample of 108 respondents using a stratified random sampling technique. Data collection was executed using a non-disguised, structured questionnaire divided into two key sections containing 22 finalized statements. Part I captured essential demographic variables (Gender, Educational Background, and Experience Level), while Part II evaluated perceived opportunities and challenges categorized across the four traditional marketing mix dimensions: Product, Price, Distribution, and Promotion. To evaluate the underlying factors and empirical relationships, descriptive statistics, factor analysis, and regression modeling were employed, complemented by independent-samples t-tests and Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) to test for statistically significant demographic variations across numerical scores (Dash et al., 2026). Statistical analyses reveal that demographic variables selectively shape rural market perceptions in tribal Odisha. Educational attainment acts as a universal determinant, significantly influencing all operational dimensions, including product, price, distribution, promotion, overall marketing, and facilitating agencies, leading to the complete rejection of all corresponding null hypotheses. Gender significantly impacts views on core operational factors such as product, price, distribution, and supporting agencies, while remaining neutral toward promotion and marketing. Ultimately, the study underscores that a robust rural marketing ecosystem, facilitating the seamless exchange of goods and services within rural regions and across rural-urban networks is imperative for overcoming operational hurdles, unlocking local market potential, and driving sustainable socioeconomic growth across Odisha's tribal lands.

detail.abstract: Directive (EU) 2024/825 on empowering consumers for the green transition seeks to address the challenges of manipulative green marketing and establish a stricter regulatory framework, ensuring better transparency of environmental claims and other essential information on product sustainability. By prohibiting unfounded and misleading environmental claims and introducing an obligation to provide information on the product's reparability score and the duration of software updates, and by preventing planned early obsolescence, the Directive seeks to contribute to sustainable development in the EU's internal market. The paper outlines new provisions on greenwashing and planned early obsolescence, accompanied by new national solutions, particularly in Croatian law, and examples from the CJEU case law and EU Member States. Following a comprehensive analysis of the rules and practice, a legitimate question has arisen regarding the effectiveness of the newly introduced solutions and shortcomings that may hinder the goals of the green transition and sustainable development.

detail.abstract: Modern retail systems have reshaped the distributive trades throughout the world, typically producing large consumer gains by displacing traditional outlets. Walmart's expansion into U.S. grocery retailing provides a different experiment: it entered a mature oligopoly of modern supermarket chains, where such gains should be smallest, yet the leading welfare estimate exceeds those documented for retail modernization in the developing world. We reconcile these findings by recognizing that consumers value proximity as well as price, and that store density is a strategic sunk investment that static welfare calculations hold fixed. We model supermarket competition as a dynamic discrete game among heterogeneous chains: incumbents decide each period whether to add or subtract stores or exit the market entirely, potential entrants choose whether to enter, and product-market competition is captured via a discrete-choice demand system in which consumers trade off price against local store density, alongside unobserved heterogeneity in chain-level quality. Resolved without Walmart, the equilibrium features rival chains entering, remaining, and building more stores, replacing much of the accessibility Walmart provided. The implied consumer gains from Walmart's entry are economically meaningful but substantially smaller than the leading estimate, restoring the ordering that the economics of retail modernization predicts.

detail.abstract: A visibility score for AI answers is a rate over a prompt set the measuring party chose and does not publish, so two parties measuring the same brand on the same engine on the same day can report different numbers. Six prompt frames, built to one brief by documented rules and three of them asking for the identical object, measured 46 US travel destinations in two substitution categories on Gemini, OpenAI and Perplexity across four captures between 6 September and 13 October 2026, from a hashed 720-prompt set fixed before the first call. A frame chosen because it most favored a destination in one measurement period still favored it in the next: by 12.43, 11.46 and 10.76 points of mention rate on Gemini over twelve, twenty-five and thirty-seven days, and by 8.54 points on OpenAI over thirty-four days with the model version pinned, against 0.83 to 1.36 points of drift when nothing is chosen. The advantage is a reordering of destinations against one another rather than a rise in the level of the market: among frames asking for the identical object the frame main effect over the 46 is 0.00 to 0.01 of systematic variance while the frame by destination interaction is 0.08 to 0.11. A factorial on 600 further prompts separates what the prompts ask about from how broadly they ask it and from how the request is phrased, and orders them in that size in all 24 combinations of engine, cluster, population and scale. Pinning the engine is not a remedy: over thirty-four days with the request byte-identical and the version string identical on all 2,880 runs, the share of answers citing a source fell from 0.620 to 0.514, and one engine withdrew the model version under measurement while continuing to publish its name. Every figure is conditional on this vertical, these 46 destinations and the levels these designs contain. No commercial product was measured.

detail.abstract: Market basket analysis (MBA) conventionally pools all customer transactions before mining association rules, implicitly assuming a homogeneous purchasing population. This study quantifies the extent to which this pooling suppresses real copurchase associations-aggregation-induced rule loss-across four customer value segments derived from Recency, Frequency, and Monetary (RFM) scoring. Using the UCI Online Retail dataset (17,087 MBA-eligible invoices, 4,334 identified customers), FP-Growth and Apriori were applied independently within each segment and compared against a global baseline. The full pipeline was replicated on a non-overlapping annual cohort (UCI Online Retail II, 2009-2010; 17,448 invoices) to assess temporal robustness. Across both cohorts, aggregate MBA consistently failed to surface at least 43% of the product associations identified by segmented analysis-reaching 54.7% in the primary cohort-while every rule it produced originated exclusively from the Champions (highest-value) segment. All 125 segmented rules in the primary dataset and all 91 in the replication survived Bonferroni correction (100% in both cohorts), confirming that the invisible associations are statistically real. A 21-point sensitivity grid confirmed threshold stability of the primary invisible-rule fraction (within ±10 percentage points across support 0.010-0.025; maximum observed deviation-8.9pp). Cross-period comparison revealed two qualitatively distinct forms of aggregationinduced rule loss: structural suppression, in which pooling genuinely weakens measured associations, and threshold-induced loss, in which rules fall marginally below the global support cutoff. The findings provide empirical quantification of the aggregation bias theorised by Boztug and Reutterer (2008) across two independent retail cohorts.

detail.abstract: Firms can influence consumer decisions by choosing which questions come first. I study the welfare consequences when firms and consumers prefer different outcomes. Choices satisfy three requirements for free will: openness, development through answering questions, and responsiveness to values. I bound consumption losses from transferring control to the firm and show how experimentation can select the most harmful tested sequence. Authority to refuse preceding interactions can have value even when choices are unchanged. A simulated cancellation experiment illustrates how consumer losses can accompany higher profits and total surplus.

detail.abstract: This study provides a rigorous macroeconomic, fiscal, and institutional evaluation of Universal Basic Income (UBI) in India within the context of accelerating artificial intelligence (AI) automation. Integrating task-based capital-labour substitution theory (Acemoglu & Restrepo, 2020) with the framework of premature deindustrialization (Rodrik, 2016), we develop a granular sectoral exposure model revealing that generative AI disproportionately threatens India's high-productivity service export engines (IT-BPM and BFSI), while informal labour absorption remains structurally depressed. Updating the seminal parameters of the Economic Survey 2016-17 to FY 2026-27 macroeconomic fundamentals (nominal GDP of ₹356 lakh crore), we simulate five distinct cash transfer architectures. A Full Universal UBI (₹2,000/month/adult) demands 6.4% of GDP (gross), exceeding nearterm fiscal limits. In contrast, a Targeted Quasi-UBI delivering ₹1,500/month to the bottom 40% of adults (~380 million citizens) requires 1.9% of GDP gross and only 0.4% of GDP net if regressive non-merit subsidies (estimated at 4.2% of GDP by NIPFP) are systematically rationalized. Grounded in constitutional jurisprudence under Articles 14 and 21, and leveraging the matured JAM Trinity 2.0 (540M+ PMJDY accounts, >98% Aadhaar coverage, 15B+ monthly UPI transactions), we propose a tri-phasic policy implementation roadmap (2026-2035) supported by a Sovereign AI & Compute Dividend Fund. We conclude that an unconditional income floor represents an indispensable macroeconomic stabilizer against capital-biased technological change in the Global South.

detail.abstract: A purchase made by voice through software agents is spread across a spoken exchange and transaction objects held by different agents. When the consumer later disputes an order, asks what was said about allergens, or wants to withdraw, someone has to show what was asked, what was answered, on which information, and what was approved. This position paper reads, against one scenario, the specifications that a voice purchase now crosses: a protocol for handing a conversation between agents, two recent protocols for the channel between a consumer's agent and a company's agent, three agentic commerce protocols, an emerging format for conversation records, and proposed work on auditing agents. None of these eight specifications, in the versions read, defines a link between the conversation, the transaction objects and the merchant information the agents relied on, or a way for such a record to reach the consumer. European Union consumer and food information law sets what the consumer must be told before the order and requires a durable confirmation after it, but not a record of the conversation. The paper separates those obligations from the evidence a trader needs to show compliance, derives five requirements on records, and proposes, as evidence for disputes, a minimal purchase record with three typed references, to the conversation, to the transaction and to the merchant declarations, delivered differently to the consumer, the trader and an auditor. It closes with extension points for each specification.

detail.abstract: Greater urgency in renewable expansion has driven a corresponding rise in the cost of policy incentives. Can the rollout be accelerated while enhancing policy efficiency? This analysis finds that the current RPS-REC scheme clears only a baseline cost-benefit test, leaving room for improvement. detail.abstract:
Korean Abstract:
재생에너지 보급 확대가 시급한 가운데, 이를 촉진할 보조금의 부담도 가중되고 있다. 과연 보급 가속화와 정책 효율화라는 두 목표를 동시에 달성할 수 있을까? 분석 결과, 현행 보조금 제도(RPS-REC)는 최소한의 경제적 타당성을 갖추었으나 여전히 개선의 여지가 있다. 더욱이 전력계통 연결 지연과 자본조달 제약의 구조적 병목이 서로 맞물리면서 보급을 지연시키고 있어, 보조금의 효율성마저 떨어질 수 있다. 결국 보급 속도와 효율성을 동시에 확보하려면 보조금 제도의 합리화, 전력계통 확충, 자본조달 환경 정비가 빠짐없이 통합적으로 추진될 필요가 있다.

English Abstract:
Greater urgency in renewable expansion has driven a corresponding rise in the cost of policy incentives. Can the rollout be accelerated while enhancing policy efficiency? This analysis finds that the current RPS-REC scheme clears only a baseline cost-benefit test, leaving room for improvement. Interlocking bottlenecks in grid connection and financing slow renewable deployment and risk eroding the cost-effectiveness of subsidies. Achieving both speed and efficiency will require coordinated progress on three fronts: rationalizing subsidy design, expanding grid infrastructure, and improving financing conditions.

title: Beyond the Prompt: AI Can Do the Marketing Work-But Can It Be the Marketer? A Conceptual Perspective on the Evolving Role of the Marketing Manager

detail.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) and emerging agentic AI systems are rapidly transforming marketing by automating activities traditionally performed by marketing professionals, including market analysis, content creation, customer segmentation, personalization, campaign optimization, and performance evaluation. As AI systems become capable of executing increasingly complex sequences of marketing tasks, an important question emerges: what remains distinctive about the role of the Marketing Manager? This conceptual paper examines the evolving relationship between artificial intelligence and marketing management through the lens of accountability theory, which holds that being answerable to an audience for a decision changes how a person reasons about it. Drawing on recent research in artificial intelligence, marketing, organizational decision-making, creativity, and human-AI collaboration, the paper argues that AI is not simply automating marketing activities but redistributing managerial responsibility toward a core of functions that accountability makes distinctly human: setting organizational direction, interpretation, prioritization, integration, judgment, and accountability itself. Four propositions are developed: AI substitution potential rises with task structure, repetitiveness, and data intensity; the value of human managerial involvement rises with ambiguity, contextual interpretation, and competing objectives; human-AI collaboration is most valuable when AI expands the decision space while managers retain interpretation and prioritization; and as AI capability increases, the manager's contribution shifts from direct task execution toward direction-setting, orchestration, judgment, and accountability. The paper also considers, as a contextual extension rather than an established finding, whether these dynamics might operate with particular visibility in markets such as the GCC and MENA region, where rapid AI adoption, audience heterogeneity, and familybusiness governance structures are commonly reported. The paper contributes to the emerging literature on AI-enabled marketing by positioning the Marketing Manager as an orchestrator of AI-enabled capability, reframing the future of marketing management from a replacement perspective toward a model of accountable, augmented managerial capability.

affiliations.org_name: Unaffiliated Authors - affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.abstract: Speech audiometry is a routine part of hearing-aid (HA) audiologists’ clinical practice, yet no international consensus exists on which speech materials or masking conditions should be used. In France, a large-scale reform of hearing-aid reimbursement (100 % Santé, 2018) has established speech audiometry in noise as a criterion for prescribing hearing aids and a mandatory component of post-fitting assessment, and two sentence-in-noise tests have entered clinical use since the previous national survey by Rembaud et al. (2017). To document current practice and test whether it has evolved, we conducted an online survey of HA audiologists practising in France between February and June 2024 (N = 266). The questionnaire covered the speech materials and masking conditions used in speech audiometry, complementary auditory tests, and cognitive-screening tools. Word-based materials dominated overall, driven by the Fournier disyllabic lists (used by 82 % of respondents), but sentence-based materials dominated for speech-in-noise assessment, with the recently distributed VRB test being the single most frequently used (35.6 % of rank-1 mentions). Cocktail-party noise was near-universal, whereas artificial and ecological noises were used by fewer than half of respondents. Cognitive screening was performed by only 14.3 % of respondents at least occasionally, despite 88 % rating cognition as strongly influencing speech-in-noise audiometry outcomes. Between-survey comparisons with 2017 revealed substantial increases in the use of masking noise (+18.8 pts) and suprathreshold audiometry (+19.0 pts), whereas stereo balancing did not change measurably.

title: The Ghost of Justice Philip Waki: Has Kenya Outgrown, or Merely Institutionalized, State-Sponsored Goonism?

detail.title: The Ghost of Justice Philip Waki: Has Kenya Outgrown, or Merely Institutionalized, State-Sponsored Goonism?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NONE

keywords: Commission of Inquiry into Post-Election Violence (CIPEV)

detail.abstract: On 15 October 2008, Justice Philip Waki delivered to President Mwai Kibaki and the Panel of Eminent African Personalities a 529page indictment of Kenya's political culture: the Report of the Commission of Inquiry into Post-Election Violence (CIPEV), which determined that the deaths of at least 1,133 Kenyans following the 2007 election were attributable not to spontaneous ethnic conflict but to organised, financed and politically orchestrated violence, executed substantially by gangs recruited and remunerated by political and commercial elites. Seventeen years later, on 12 July 2026, armed men uniformly characterised in police statements and press reportage as "goons" assailed a church service and a political rally in Kisumu and Nyahururu respectively, days ahead of a parliamentary by-election in Ol Kalou, while the state security apparatus constitutionally obliged to safeguard both assemblies either failed to discharge that duty or, on credible allegation, acquiesced in its breach. This article interrogates the question its title poses directly: has Kenya outgrown the mechanism Waki diagnosed, or has it merely institutionalised it? Testing that question against the successive collapse of the domestic Special Tribunal and the International Criminal Court process, the documented recurrence of hired political violence across three subsequent electoral cycles, Kenya's constitutional guarantees under Articles 21, 37 and 244, and the 84.1 per cent probability of electoral violence a 2026 statistical index now assigns to 2027, the article concludes that Kenya has not outgrown its ghost. It has, rather, furnished the ghost a permanent address, and continues to service the tenancy.

detail.abstract: When the European Commission, indeed any competition authority, protects competition to innovate it protects competition in Future Markets, markets for products which do not exist yet.  When the Commission defines a Future Market it must apply the Future Markets Model, which simply lays out the logical steps any competition authority must take as it defines and analyzes a Future Market.  This is the only way any competition authority has or can protect dynamic competition.  Thus when the Commission says in its draft Guidelines that it will aggressively protect competition to innovate it is really saying is that it will apply the Future Markets Model aggressively.  A version of this article is available at https://www.concurrences.com/en/review/issues/no-10-2026/dossier/draft-merger-guidelines-first-review/part-ix-in-its-merger-guidelines-the-european-commission-actually-says-it-will

detail.abstract: Pancreatic neuroendocrine neoplasms (pNENs) require complex multidisciplinary decision-making because management depends on tumour biology, disease extent, functional status, treatment history and therapeutic sequencing. We developed pNEN Navigator, a disease-specific clinical decision-support system combining PNEN-LLM, curated evidence retrieval, seven specialist agents and central multidisciplinary synthesis. Evaluation comprised 200 multiple-choice questions, 300 open-ended question–answer items and 98 real-world multidisciplinary team (MDT) cases. PNEN-LLM achieved the highest multiple-choice accuracy (0.885) and macro precision (0.960), while performance across automated free-text metrics varied among systems. In the real-world cohort, pNEN Navigator showed domain-dependent agreement with recorded MDT-derived labels, with Cohen’s κ ranging from 0.260 for surgery to 0.957 for pathology or grade review; 52 of 98 cases matched the recorded MDT-derived labels in at least seven of eight decision domains. Comparative analyses further characterised domain-specific differences in recommendation patterns and agreement across AI systems. These findings provide a disease-specific, evidence-grounded multi-agent framework for evaluating multidisciplinary AI decision support at the level of explicit clinical decisions and support prospective multicentre validation.

detail.abstract: Underwater images frequently exhibit wavelength dependent color attenuation, low contrast, scattering, and loss of fine detail. The diversity of these degradations and the imperfect reference images used by existing paired datasets make a single, uniformly supervised restoration mapping unreliable. This paper presents NEREUS, a reliability aware underwater image restoration framework that combines robust color prior guidance, degradation conditioned feature processing, and prototype routed expert adaptation. A frozen percentile based color prior branch first produces a stabilized input that compensates global dynamic range and channel imbalance. At each encoder and decoder stage, a guided dynamic feature modulation block integrates multi scale image guidance, texture–context refinement, and a prototype routed mixture of experts. A learnable degradation memory supplies a global condition to the local routers, while latent conditioned gates filter skip features before reconstruction. During training, pre computed DINO feature distances are used to weight imperfect references, and a frozen DINO backbone provides feature space anchor supervision. Experiments on paired and real world non reference benchmarks show that NEREUS achieves 23.75 dB PSNR, 0.923 SSIM, and 0.093 LPIPS on UIEB/U90, and 28.86 dB PSNR, 0.916 SSIM, and 0.083 LPIPS on LSUI 400. On U90 and LSUI 400, NEREUS has the lowest LPIPS among compared methods with 10.18 M parameters and 157.56 G FLOPs at 256 × 256.

title: The Supply of Expertise: New Technologies, New Skills, and Worker Impacts
affiliations: Tilburg University, Goethe University Frankfurt and Utrecht School of Economics

detail.title: The Supply of Expertise: New Technologies, New Skills, and Worker Impacts
detail.abstract: Does educational content respond to technological advances, and do such changes enable workers to acquire new valuable expertise? We construct a novel database of legally binding training curricula spanning the near universe of vocational training in Germany over five decades, and link curriculum updates to breakthrough technologies using Natural Language Processing. We trace a causal chain from technological change to curriculum content to worker outcomes. Technological change spurs curriculum updates, and training content shifts toward less routine-intensive tasks. This shift occurs predominantly through the emergence of new skills related to social, digital, and problem-solving competencies, rather than the removal of old ones. This within-occupation margin is quantitatively important: curriculum updates account for two-thirds of the overall deroutinization in vocational skill supply over this period. Using administrative employer-employee data and a stacked difference-in-differences design, we show that new-skilled workers earn higher wages, especially in technology-exposed occupations, and are more likely to remain employed in their trained occupation. In contrast, older occupational incumbents experience wage declines, indicating skill obsolescence. These findings highlight the central role of within-occupation skill supply adjustments — not just educational attainment — in meeting evolving labor market demands.

title: Behavioral Pricing Constrains Tariff Pass-Through

detail.title: Behavioral Pricing Constrains Tariff Pass-Through

detail.abstract: How do firms transmit macroeconomic shocks to consumers through retail prices? We show that pricing frictions induced by behavioral biases play a central role in shaping how cost shocks pass-through to consumers. We document that import tariffs are transmitted primarily through prices that do not end in nine, while nine-ending prices exhibit substantially lower pass-through. After the tariffs, annual inflation is meaningfully larger for non-nine-ending priced products, even products that are not tariffed. These findings identify channels through which consumer biases constrain firms' responses to macroeconomic shocks.

detail.abstract: We study how industrial robots affect human capital investment during high school. Using Texas administrative records and an instrument based on European robot adoption, we find that exposure reduces dropout, raises observed completion, and shifts coursework toward college preparation and away from vocational subjects. Advanced coursework increases across grades, while dropout reductions and gains in quantitative coursework are concentrated in upper grades. Boys reduce vocational coursework more, narrowing gender differences in course taking, whereas girls increase advanced coursework more, widening their advantage in college preparation. Adjustment to automation is already underway in high school, through continued schooling and curricular choices.
